The table never empties, and the recreate phase fails with `UNIQUE constraint failed: wardrobe_items.id`.
- Fix: added `deleteRaw` to `WardrobeRepository` and `OutfitPresetsRepository` (mirrors the existing `createFromVault` / `findByCharacterIdRaw` bypass methods) and switched the route handler at `app/api/v1/characters/[id]/route.ts` to use `deleteRaw` for the wipe and `createFromVault` for the rebuild. Both bypass the sync chain so the loop runs to completion without re-ingesting itself.

#### Collapsible Staff-message bars in the Salon

- **New `systemKind` field.** Added a string column on `chat_messages` (Zod field on `MessageEventSchema` and `ChatMessageRowSchema`) carrying a stable kebab-case sub-classification of any Staff-authored message — e.g. `timestamp`, `project-context`, `memory-recap`, `tool-run`. Migration: `migrations/scripts/add-system-kind-field.ts` (`add-system-kind-field-v1`). Every writer now persists a `systemKind`: Lantern (`avatar` / `background` / `character-image`), Aurora (`opening-outfit` / `outfit-change`), Librarian (`opened-by-user`, `saved`, `renamed`, `summary`, etc.), Concierge (`danger`), Prospero (`connection-profile-change`, `project-context`, `tool-run`), Host (`add` / `remove` / `status-change` / `scenario` / `roster` / `timestamp` / `silent-mode-enter` / `silent-mode-exit` / `user-character` / `join-scenario`), Commonplace Book (`memory-recap` / `relevant-memories` / `inter-character-memories` / `consolidated`). Tool-run TOOL rows from `actions/tools.ts` and `actions/run-tool.ts` get `systemKind: 'tool-run'`.
- **Salon collapse UI.** Staff-authored assistant rows in the Salon now render as a thin one-line bar by default — sender display name, humanized kind label (e.g. "project information", "time"), timestamp, chevron — and expand to the full message on click. A new "collapse" chevron in the action bar reverses the state. Expansion state is tracked per-message in `expandedSystemMessageIds` on the Salon page and threaded through `VirtualizedMessageList` into `MessageRow`. Sender/kind labels live in `app/salon/[id]/components/system-message-labels.ts`. New `qt-chat-system-bar*` utility classes in `app/styles/qt-components/_chat.css` with light/dark tokens in `_variables.css`.
- **Schema/export updates.** `public/schemas/qtap-export.schema.json` and `docs/developer/DDL.md` updated for the new column.

#### Tool calls render as standalone bubbles attributed to the actor

- **All TOOL rows are standalone.** `useChatData.groupToolsWithMessages` is removed; both character-initiated and user-initiated TOOL messages render as their own row in the salon timeline. The `Message.toolCalls` field, the embedded-tool render block in `MessageRow`, and the `embedded` prop on `ToolMessage` are removed as dead code.
- **Character attribution.** `saveToolMessages` in `lib/services/chat-message/tool-execution.service.ts` now persists the responding character's `participantId` on TOOL rows; both call sites (`message-finalizer.service.ts` and `orchestrator.service.ts`) pass it through. `VirtualizedMessageList` resolves `headerAvatar` via `getMessageAvatar`, falling back to the most recent ASSISTANT row's participant when the TOOL message predates the participantId persistence change.
- **Unified `ToolMessage` header.** `ToolMessage` now takes a single `headerAvatar` prop (replacing `systemAvatar`) and renders a consistent layout: the author avatar on the left, the author name (Prospero or the character) in the header, an `actor ran <tool>` line below it, and the existing collapsible Request/Response panes. For Prospero rows the actor is the operator (`toolData.operatorName`); for character rows the actor name matches the header and is suppressed below it to avoid duplication.

#### User-initiated tool runs are Prospero bubbles

- **Standalone Prospero rendering.** TOOL messages produced by the Run Tool modal are no longer visually grouped into the user's bubble. `useChatData.groupToolsWithMessages` only groups character-initiated TOOL messages under the preceding ASSISTANT message; user-initiated TOOL messages render as their own row.
- **Prospero authorship.** `app/api/v1/chats/[id]/actions/run-tool.ts` now persists `systemSender: 'prospero'` on the TOOL message and embeds the operator's display name (`user.name || user.username`) in the JSON content. `VirtualizedMessageList` passes a `systemAvatar` prop to `ToolMessage`; the standalone layout swaps the muted tool-icon circle for the Prospero portrait and shows a "{operatorName} ran `{toolName}`" attribution under "Prospero". Existing collapsible Request/Response panes with individual copy buttons are unchanged.
- **Private (whisper) toggle.** `RunToolModal` has a new "Private (whisper)" checkbox (default off). When checked, the API writes the operator's userId into `targetParticipantIds`. The userId is a UUID but never a participant ID, so the salon visibility filter at `app/salon/[id]/page.tsx` hides the bubble unless "show all whispers" is on, and `filterWhisperMessages` excludes it from every character's LLM context.
- **Single-character context honors TOOL whispers.** `lib/services/chat-message/context-builder.service.ts` now drops TOOL messages with non-empty `targetParticipantIds` that don't include the responding character before building conversation messages, so private runs don't leak into single-character chats (multi-character mode already filtered via `filterWhisperMessages` in the context manager).

#### Per-character Librarian summaries

- **Summaries are now whispered, not broadcast.** The Librarian still regenerates `chat.contextSummary` at the same checkpoints (used by title generation, danger classification, story background, etc.), but the conversation-summary message in the transcript is now produced once per LLM-controlled CHARACTER participant and whispered privately to them via `targetParticipantIds`. Each character may have entered mid-chat or stepped away and back, so each gets a summary tailored to what they actually saw.
- **Visible-slice computation.** For each participant, the summary input is built by composing (1) the existing `filterMessagesByHistoryAccess` slice (skip messages before they joined unless `hasHistoryAccess === true`), (2) a new presence-window slice that drops messages during periods they were `absent` or `removed`, and (3) the existing `filterWhisperMessages` step. Presence windows are computed from Host status announcements — see the new `computePresenceWindowsForParticipant` and `filterMessagesByPresenceWindows` helpers in `lib/chat/context/message-attribution.ts`.
- **Host status announcements now carry structured data.** Added `hostEvent` JSON column on `chat_messages` (`{ participantId, toStatus }`) plus a Zod field on `MessageEventSchema` and `ChatMessageRowSchema`. `postHostAddAnnouncement` / `postHostRemoveAnnouncement` / `postHostStatusChangeAnnouncement` in `lib/services/host-notifications/writer.ts` now require `participantId` and persist `hostEvent`. Migration: `migrations/scripts/add-host-event-field.ts` (`add-host-event-field-v1`). Other Host announcements (scenario, roster, timestamp, silent-mode, join-scenario) leave `hostEvent` NULL.
- **Call sites updated** in `app/api/v1/chats/route.ts`, `app/api/v1/chats/[id]/helpers.ts`, and `app/api/v1/chats/[id]/actions/participants.ts` to pass `participantId` (and `initialStatus` for adds). The add path was reordered so the new participant is resolved before the Host announcement fires.
- **Old whispered summaries are swept.** When a fresh per-character summary whisper is posted, prior Librarian summary whispers targeted at the same participant are deleted from the chat. Identified by `systemSender === 'librarian'`, exact single-target match, and the new `SUMMARY_CONTENT_PREFIX` content marker. Old broadcast summaries (from before this change) are not touched.
- **New repository helper.** `chats.repository.ts` and `lib/repositories/user-scoped.ts` expose `deleteMessagesByIds(chatId, ids[])`; underlying op added on `chats-messages.ops.ts`.
- **Reuse-when-equal optimization.** When a participant's visible slice contains exactly the same message IDs that fed the global summary (single-character chats with no absences and no whispers, etc.), the global summary text is reused verbatim rather than calling the cheap LLM again.
- **Catch-up summary on join.** When a character is added to a chat with `hasHistoryAccess === true`, `triggerCatchUpSummaryAsync` fires in the background to whisper a summary of prior history to the joining character right away — they don't have to wait for the next checkpoint. No-op when `hasHistoryAccess` is false; that case waits for the next regular regen.
- **Writer signature change.** `postLibrarianSummaryAnnouncement` now accepts `targetParticipantIds`. The exported `SUMMARY_CONTENT_PREFIX` constant is the canonical body marker for sweeping prior summaries.

#### System Prompt Refactor (Phase A + B + C + D + E + F + G + H + I)

Begun the move of dynamic state out of the per-turn system prompt and into Staff-authored ASSISTANT messages, so the system prompt can become a static, cache-friendly artifact and the chat transcript can become the single source of truth for state changes.

- **New Staff persona — the Commonplace Book.** Added `commonplaceBook` to the `systemSender` enum in `lib/schemas/chat.types.ts`, `lib/database/repositories/chats-messages.ops.ts`, `app/salon/[id]/types.ts`, and `public/schemas/qtap-export.schema.json`. New writer module at `lib/services/commonplace-notifications/writer.ts` exports `postCommonplaceWhisper` (persistent path) and `voiceCommonplaceContent` (per-turn voicing helper). Avatar at `public/images/avatars/commonplace-book-avatar.webp` wired into `getMessageAvatar` in `app/salon/[id]/page.tsx`. No database migration needed — the `chat_messages.systemSender` column has no CHECK constraint.
- **Memory tail moved out of the system prompt.** The memory recap, relevant memories, and inter-character memories used to be concatenated onto the system prompt. They are now persisted as a single consolidated Commonplace Book whisper per turn — voiced in the steampunk Quilltap style ("*The Commonplace Book lays open at your bookmark…*") — visible in the salon UI right after the user's message that triggered it, with the Commonplace Book avatar. For the LLM call, the same recall content is inlined into the new user message body in plain second-person framing ("You remember the following entries that bear on this moment: …") — no Staff persona, no meta-narrative, no consecutive-assistant alternation issue. Past Commonplace Book whispers are filtered out of `existingMessages` before context building (they live in the transcript for the user, but the LLM gets fresh recall each turn). The memories table remains the source of truth.
- **System transparency filter no longer drops Staff messages.** For opaque characters (`systemTransparency !== true`), `lib/services/chat-message/context-builder.service.ts` now strips the `systemSender` attribution but keeps the message body, so the LLM still receives content (scenario, status, memory) as a generic assistant line. Previously, opaque characters lost the message entirely. The salon UI is unaffected — the human user always sees Staff-attributed messages with their avatars.
- **Host content moved out of the system prompt (Phase C wire-up).** Scenario, user-character introduction, multi-character roster, own-status reminder, silent-mode rule, recent status changes, and join-scenario context now ship as Host-authored ASSISTANT messages in the chat transcript instead of being concatenated onto the per-turn system prompt.
  - **At chat creation** (`createInitialMessages` in `app/api/v1/chats/route.ts`): right after the SYSTEM message, the Host posts the scenario announcement (if a scenario is set), the user-character introduction (if a user character is configured), and — for multi-character chats — a welcome announcement for each LLM-controlled CHARACTER participant so each character learns about the others from the transcript.
  - **At participant add** (`processChatUpdates` in `app/api/v1/chats/[id]/helpers.ts` and `handleAddParticipantAction` in `app/api/v1/chats/[id]/actions/participants.ts`): when a new participant has a non-empty `joinScenario` and `hasHistoryAccess === false`, the Host posts a private join-scenario whisper targeted at the joining participant via `targetParticipantIds`. Replaces the per-turn `## How You Entered This Conversation` insertion.
  - **At silent-mode transitions** (`handleParticipantUpdate` in `app/api/v1/chats/[id]/helpers.ts`): when a participant transitions into or out of silent mode, the Host posts a private silent-mode entry or exit whisper carrying the full silent-mode rule directly to the affected character. - **Phase H — precompiled identity stack.** Each chat now carries a per-participant cache of the character-static portion of the system prompt (`chats.compiledIdentityStacks`, JSON, keyed by participantId). The cached body — preamble + base prompt + personality + aliases + pronouns + physical descriptions + example dialogues, with `{{user}}` / `{{scenario}}` / `{{persona}}` resolved — feeds directly into the per-turn `buildSystemPrompt`, which wraps it with the chat-level roleplay template, tool instructions, and tool reinforcement. The LLM provider now sees a stable cache-friendly prefix across turns within a chat session.
  - **Schema** added at `lib/schemas/chat.types.ts` (`compiledIdentityStacks: JsonSchema.nullable().optional()`) on both `ChatMetadataSchema` and `ChatMetadataBaseSchema`. SQLite column added at `docs/developer/DDL.md` (chats table, `"compiledIdentityStacks" TEXT DEFAULT NULL`). Migration: `migrations/scripts/add-compiled-identity-stacks-field.ts` (id `add-compiled-identity-stacks-field-v1`), registered in `migrations/scripts/index.ts`. The field is excluded from `.qtap` exports — it's a derivable cache, and on import the read-through fallback in `buildSystemPrompt` rebuilds it on the first turn.
  - **New module** `lib/services/system-prompt-compiler/compiler.ts` exports `getCompiledIdentityStack`, `compileAllIdentityStacks`, and `compileIdentityStackForParticipant`. Errors never propagate — failures log and the read-through fallback covers them.
  - **Builder split.** `buildSystemPrompt` was refactored: a new `buildIdentityStack(options)` produces just the static portion, and `buildSystemPrompt` accepts an optional `precompiledIdentityStack` and uses it verbatim when supplied (the cache-hit path), otherwise calls `buildIdentityStack` (read-through fallback). The order of the per-turn additions was also adjusted so the static identity stack leads, with the dynamic roleplay template / tool instructions / tool reinforcement appended after it — this puts the stable bytes up front and the changing bytes at the end, maximizing provider prompt-cache hits.
  - **Compile triggers.** `compileAllIdentityStacks` runs in `app/api/v1/chats/route.ts` `handleCreate` after `repos.chats.create`. `compileIdentityStackForParticipant` runs in `app/api/v1/chats/[id]/helpers.ts` (after `handleAddParticipant` succeeds in `processChatUpdates`, and after `selectedSystemPromptId` changes via `handleParticipantUpdate`) and in `app/api/v1/chats/[id]/actions/participants.ts` (after the action-dispatch add path and the soft-deleted reactivation path). On `controlledBy` flip (a participant becoming user-controlled or LLM-controlled) the whole map is recompiled because that affects `{{user}}` / `{{persona}}` for every other participant.
  - **Read path.** `lib/chat/context-manager.ts` looks up the cached stack for `respondingParticipant` via `getCompiledIdentityStack` and forwards it as `precompiledIdentityStack` to `buildSystemPrompt`. To make the cache lookup work for single-character chats too, the orchestrator → context-builder → context-manager pipeline now passes `respondingParticipant: characterParticipant` always (previously gated on `isMultiCharacter`).
  - **Known limitation.** Edits to the underlying character record (name, personality, aliases, pronouns, physical descriptions, example dialogues, `systemPrompts`) do NOT auto-invalidate cached stacks across chats — that fan-out is its own design pass. Until it lands, users editing a character mid-chat will keep seeing the stack from compile time. Workaround: read-through fallback ensures correctness when the cached entry is null/missing for a participant, so a future "rehydrate this chat" admin button can simply clear the map.
  - **Tests** added at `__tests__/unit/context-management.test.ts` covering the cache-hit path (precompiled stack used verbatim, character body NOT rebuilt), the cache-miss/fallback path (empty stack triggers fresh build), and the new ordering (identity stack → roleplay template → tool instructions → tool reinforcement).

### 4.3.1

#### Bug Fixes

- **SQLite journal mode default changed from WAL to TRUNCATE**: Quilltap data directories are commonly placed inside cloud-synced folders (iCloud Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive, Google Drive). WAL mode keeps `.db-wal` and `.db-shm` files alongside the main `.db`; if those files sync out of order with the main database — which all four providers can do, especially on dirty shutdown — the database can be corrupted or lose recent writes on the next open. Switching to `TRUNCATE` keeps the rollback journal in a single auxiliary file that is truncated to zero on every commit, eliminating the multi-file sync hazard. Existing databases auto-migrate on first open after upgrade (SQLite checkpoints any pre-existing WAL into the main file as part of the journal-mode transition). The change applies to all three databases — main (`quilltap.db`), LLM logs (`quilltap-llm-logs.db`), and mount index (`quilltap-mount-index.db`) — plus the meta-table connection used during startup.
- **`SQLITE_WAL_MODE` env var inverted**: Previously `SQLITE_WAL_MODE=false` was the opt-out; now `SQLITE_WAL_MODE=true` is the opt-in. Set this only when the data directory lives on a fast local SSD that is not synced to the cloud.
- **Internal**: `lib/startup/db-encryption-converter.ts` now leaves freshly-encrypted databases in TRUNCATE mode rather than WAL, matching the new resting state.

- **Scriptorium / Aurora — post-Librarian code cleanup**: Removed dead code and fixed several issues introduced in the refactor since commit `0e13b2f`:
  - `app/api/v1/chats/[id]/actions/documents.ts`: Removed local `getErrorMessage` function that duplicated the one exported from `@/lib/errors` — replaced with an import.
  - `app/aurora/[id]/edit/components/CharacterBasicInfo.tsx`: The `overlayManagedDisabled = false` constant was always `false` (vault-managed fields intentionally stay editable), so all `disabled={overlayManagedDisabled}` props and `{!overlayManagedDisabled && …}` guards were dead code. Removed the constant and unwrapped/simplified all callsites. `Add First Scenario` empty-state button now uses `[...formData.scenarios, newScenario]` for consistency with the header button.
  - `app/scriptorium/[id]/components/FileTable.tsx`: (1) Extracted `isBlobBacked(fileType)` helper to remove a three-way type-equality check repeated in three places. (2) Merged two consecutive `if` blocks in `toggleExpand` (one for `'blob'` and one for `'pdf' | 'docx'`) into a single call guarded by the helper. (3) Changed `<>` keyless fragments wrapping `<tr>` pairs to `<Fragment key={file.id}>` so React has a stable root key for each mapped row. (4) `FileDetailRow` is now keyed by `blob?.updatedAt ?? 'loading'` so its local `description` state resets when blob metadata loads rather than staying frozen at its empty-string initial value. (5) `loadBlobDetail` had `blobDetails` in its `useCallback` dependency array, causing the callback (and `toggleExpand` which depends on it) to re-create on every blob load — replaced with `blobFetchedRef` (`useRef(new Set<string>())`) so the already-fetched guard is a stable ref; the ID is added before the first `await` to prevent duplicate concurrent requests. (6) Renamed `uploadError` state to `operationError` since it is also set by delete and description-save failures.

#### Fixes

- **Scriptorium — `doc_read_file`, `doc_write_file`, `doc_str_replace`, and `doc_copy_file` no longer reject every existing file as a boundary escape when the data directory lives behind a symlink**: `lib/doc-edit/path-resolver.ts` was realpathing the *file* path (which expands symlinks) but comparing it against an unresolved `baseDir` (which does not), so on macOS instances rooted at `~/iCloud` (a symlink to `~/Library/Mobile Documents/com~apple~CloudDocs`) the containment check rejected every file that actually existed on disk with `Path escapes project boundary` / `Path escapes general storage boundary` / `Path escapes mount point boundary`. New files (writes to a not-yet-created path) slipped through because both sides fell back to `path.resolve` without expansion. `safeRealpath` now walks up to the deepest existing ancestor, realpaths it, and re-attaches the missing tail — so a write to a brand-new file resolves consistently with its parent. `resolveProjectPath`, `resolveGeneralPath`, and the filesystem branch of `resolveDocumentStorePath` now realpath both `baseDir` and the joined path before the boundary check, and the returned `basePath` is the realpath'd value. The traversal protections (rejecting `..` segments and absolute paths) still run up front and are unchanged. New regression suite at `__tests__/unit/lib/doc-edit/path-resolver.test.ts` builds a real symlinked tmp tree and asserts that an existing project file with a space in its folder name resolves correctly, that a not-yet-created project file resolves without a boundary error, that `..` and absolute paths are still rejected, and that the same fix applies to general scope. (`lib/doc-edit/path-resolver.ts`, `__tests__/unit/lib/doc-edit/path-resolver.test.ts`)

- **Imported characters now get a vault provisioned during the import**: Characters created via `executeImport` in `lib/import/quilltap-import-service.ts` (the path used by Aurora's "Summon from Lore" wizard, regular `.qtap` imports, and the seed-data import) were not having a character vault provisioned. The only callers of `provisionVaultInBackground` lived in the `POST /api/v1/characters` route handler, so import-created characters had no `characterDocumentMountPointId` until the next server restart, when `backfillCharacterVaults` would sweep them up. During that gap, the Scriptorium and any vault-aware tooling could not see them. `importCharacters` now awaits a new `provisionImportedCharacterVault` helper after each `repos.characters.create` call (both the duplicate path and the normal/overwrite path). Vault-provisioning failures are recorded as import warnings instead of aborting the import; the startup backfill remains the safety net since `ensureCharacterVault` is idempotent. (`lib/import/quilltap-import-service.ts`)

- **Initial-greeting LLM call now writes to `llm_logs`**: `generateGreetingMessage` in `lib/chat/initial-greeting.ts` had been calling `providerClient.streamMessage` directly with no `logLLMCall` wrapper, so the LLM call that produces a chat's auto-generated opening message never showed up in the LLM Logs view (and was invisible to token/cost tracking). The function now accepts optional `userId`/`chatId`/`characterId` from the caller, wraps the stream loop in try/finally, and writes one `llm_logs` row per attempt with type `CHAT_MESSAGE` — including stream errors and any partially-accumulated content. Each of the four retry attempts in `autoGenerateFirstMessage` (full context, no-memories, Concierge uncensored fallback, plain retry) now logs its own row. Logging failures are caught and warned; they never break greeting generation. (`lib/chat/initial-greeting.ts`, `app/api/v1/chats/route.ts`)

- **Backup — character plugin data, conversation annotations, and user-installed themes were not backed up**: The ZIP backup system was missing three categories of user data. `character_plugin_data` rows (per-character plugin metadata such as Commonplace Book entries) were not collected or restored. `conversation_annotations` rows (per-message annotations added during roleplay via the Scriptorium annotation tools) were excluded. User-installed theme bundles (directories in `<data-dir>/themes/`, installed from registries or manually) were not copied into or out of backup archives. All three are now included: JSON data files `data/character-plugin-data.json` and `data/conversation-annotations.json` are written during backup and parsed (with backward-compatible fallback) during restore; a `themes/` directory mirrors `<data-dir>/themes/` (excluding `.cache/`) in the backup archive and is restored over the existing themes directory. UUID remapping in new-account mode correctly remaps `characterId` on plugin data records and `chatId`/`sourceMessageId` on annotation records. Manifest counts updated with `characterPluginData`, `conversationAnnotations`, and `userInstalledThemes` fields. (`lib/backup/backup-service.ts`, `lib/backup/restore-service.ts`, `lib/backup/types.ts`, `docs/BACKUP-RESTORE.md`, `help/system-backup-restore.md`)

New file `__tests__/unit/lib/services/chat-message/agent-mode-guardrail.test.ts` (10 tests) covers `buildAgentModeInstructions` instruction text and the ghost-wrap-up detection condition (6 cases). - **qt-* compliance pass on all new UI components since 4.3-dev start**: Updated `qt-page-title` CSS to match the established `text-3xl font-semibold leading-tight` pattern used across all page `<h1>` headings (the previous definition `text-2xl font-bold tracking-tight` was never applied anywhere). Applied `qt-page-title`, `qt-section-title`, `qt-label`, `qt-body`, `qt-body-sm`, `qt-dialog-title`, and `qt-action` in place of raw Tailwind typography classes in: `app/scriptorium/page.tsx`, `app/scriptorium/[id]/page.tsx`, `app/scriptorium/[id]/components/FileTable.tsx`, `app/scriptorium/components/DocumentStoreCard.tsx`, `app/scriptorium/components/CreateDocumentStoreDialog.tsx`, `app/scriptorium/components/EditDocumentStoreDialog.tsx`, `app/prospero/[id]/components/ScenariosCard.tsx`, `app/prospero/[id]/components/DocumentStoresCard.tsx`, `components/new-chat/CharacterPickerPanel.tsx`, `components/new-chat/NewChatForm.tsx`, `components/new-chat/NewChatModal.tsx`. (`app/styles/qt-components/_typography.css`)

- **Aurora — vault-only wardrobe items no longer disappear when an LLM creates new ones**: When a character has the document-store overlay on, dropping a `Wardrobe/<title>.md` file into the vault (via Document Mode or by hand) creates a "vault-only" wardrobe item — the read overlay surfaces it with a deterministic UUID derived from the file path, but no row exists in the `wardrobe_items` table. Observed on Friday, chat `9de8d63d-895b-452c-a423-a087c842ae26`: the user authored `Wardrobe/Dressing Gown.md` for Gary, equipped it (now possible via the recent `findByIdForCharacter` fix), then asked Friday to dress him; the LLM called `create_wardrobe_item` four times for new items and the dressing gown vanished. Cause: `WardrobeRepository.create` triggers `syncCharacterVaultWardrobe`, which calls `projectArrayIntoVaultFolder` to project the DB items into `Wardrobe/`. The projection sweep deletes any file whose path isn't in the DB-derived list, so vault-only files (with no DB row) get wiped on every wardrobe write. Same hole on `update`/`archive`/`unarchive`/`delete`, and on the symmetric outfit-presets path. Fix: `performVaultWardrobeSync` now runs a new `ingestVaultOnlyWardrobeIntoDb` step before projecting, which reads the vault snapshot, finds items/presets whose IDs aren't yet in the DB, and inserts them with `WardrobeRepository.createFromVault` / `OutfitPresetsRepository.createFromVault` — both new public methods that wrap `_create` with explicit `id`/`createdAt`/`updatedAt` and skip the post-write sync trigger to avoid recursion. The DB row picks up the same deterministic UUID the read overlay was already returning, so the equip handler's `equippedOutfit` reference stays valid across the sync. The two new methods are scoped to vault-ingestion and don't change the outward surface of `create()`. Per-item failures in the ingestion loop log a warning and continue — losing one item to a validation error is better than aborting the sync and clobbering the whole vault on the projection step. Existing already-deleted vault files in chats hit by this bug aren't restored automatically; recreate the file in Document Mode and the next sync will preserve it. New regression tests in `__tests__/unit/lib/database/repositories/character-properties-overlay.test.ts` cover the vault-only-survives-sync path and the no-op-when-already-in-DB path. (`lib/database/repositories/character-properties-overlay.ts`, `lib/database/repositories/wardrobe.repository.ts`, `lib/database/repositories/outfit-presets.repository.ts`)
- **Salon — opening a missing document now shows a toast instead of the dev error overlay**: Clicking a Document Mode entry whose underlying file no longer exists used to throw inside `useDocumentMode.openDocument` and surface a Next.js red-screen "Console Error" overlay reading `{"error":"File not found: <path>"}` (observed when Friday's `Wardrobe/Dressing Gown.md` got swept by the now-fixed projection bug). Two changes. (1) `app/api/v1/chats/[id]/actions/documents.ts` returns 404 instead of 400 for the missing-file case in `open-document`, and uses `errorResponse(message, 404)` for the `read-document` ENOENT branch as well — `notFound()` would have appended " not found" producing the awkward "File not found: X not found". (2) `useDocumentMode.openDocument` now catches the failure, formats a friendly single-line message via a new `friendlyOpenDocumentError` helper (parses the JSON server response, recognizes `"File not found"`, falls back to the raw text), shows it via `showErrorToast`, and logs the raw error with `console.warn` so it doesn't trip Next's dev-overlay-on-`console.error` behavior. (`app/api/v1/chats/[id]/actions/documents.ts`, `app/salon/[id]/hooks/useDocumentMode.ts`)
- **Prospero — `update_outfit_item` tool now resolves vault-only wardrobe items**: The sibling fix to the salon equip-handler bug. `lib/tools/handlers/wardrobe-update-outfit-handler.ts` had four raw `repos.wardrobe.findById` calls that bypassed the document-store overlay: the preset archived-item check (line 127), the preset-application loop (line 150), the by-ID equip lookup (line 208), and the coverage-summary helper (line 457). When an LLM called `update_outfit_item` with `item_id` for a vault-resident item — or applied a preset whose slots referenced vault items — the lookup returned null and the tool either threw "Wardrobe item not found" or silently fell back to `updateEquippedSlot` without displacement, leaving stale slots behind. All four call sites now use `findByIdForCharacter(characterId, id)` (added in the prior salon-equip fix), which routes through the overlay and falls back to archetype lookups for shared items. `buildCoverageSummaryFromState` gained a `characterId` parameter so its per-slot lookups can join the overlay path; the three caller sites pass `context.characterId` through. The redundant ownership check that ran after the by-ID lookup (`item.characterId != null && item.characterId !== context.characterId`) was unreachable post-fix — `findByIdForCharacter` only returns items owned by this character or archetypes (characterId null) — and was removed. New regression test in `__tests__/unit/lib/tools/handlers/wardrobe-handlers.test.ts` exercises the vault-only equip path with `findById` mocked to null and verifies the tool succeeds via `findByIdForCharacter`. (`lib/tools/handlers/wardrobe-update-outfit-handler.ts`)
- **Salon — equipping a vault-only wardrobe item from the chat UI no longer 404s**: `WardrobeRepository.findById` and `findByIds` go straight to the `wardrobe_items` table and don't consult the document-store overlay, so items that exist only as `Wardrobe/<title>.md` files in a character vault (their UUIDs are derived from path, not stored in the DB) couldn't be resolved. The salon's `useOutfit` hook listed them via `findByCharacterId` (overlay-aware), but `POST /api/v1/chats/[id]?action=equip` validated incoming IDs with the raw `findById` and returned 404 — observed on Friday, chat `9de8d63d-895b-452c-a423-a087c842ae26`, character Gary, item `c52b1e29-6a6b-84a6-8084-d5b1d0bf4d7d`. The displacement helpers had the same blind spot: `equipWithDisplacement`/`unequipWithDisplacement` used `findById` to look up the item being displaced, so swapping out a vault-resident dress (`types: ['top', 'bottom']`) for another vault item left the bottom slot stuck. Added `WardrobeRepository.findByIdForCharacter(characterId, id)` and `findByIdsForCharacter(characterId, ids)` that go through `getOverlaidWardrobeItems` and fall back to a raw lookup for archetypes (characterId null) so shared items remain reachable. Updated the equip handler (both the initial validation and the outfit-change notification's title lookup) and the displacement helpers' `DisplacementRepos` interface to use the new methods; `findById`/`findByIds` themselves stay raw-DB for export and vault-populator paths that need the canonical row. Existing displacement tests updated for the new mock shape; new regression test in `__tests__/unit/app/api/v1/chats/[id]/actions/outfit.test.ts` covers the vault-only ID round-trip. The LLM-side `update_outfit_item` tool handler in `lib/tools/handlers/wardrobe-update-outfit-handler.ts` still calls `findById` directly at four sites and is a sibling bug not covered here. (`lib/database/repositories/wardrobe.repository.ts`, `lib/wardrobe/outfit-displacement.ts`, `app/api/v1/chats/[id]/actions/outfit.ts`)
- **Salon — Host now announces participant adds and removes that come through the consolidated PUT chat-update endpoint**: The Add Character dialog calls `PUT /api/v1/chats/{id}?action=add-participant` with `{ addParticipant: {...} }`, but `add-participant` (and `remove-participant`) are only registered on the POST action dispatch in `app/api/v1/chats/[id]/handlers/post.ts`. PUT requests with those action params fell through to `handlePut` → `processChatUpdates` in `helpers.ts`, which called the lower-level `handleAddParticipant` / `handleRemoveParticipant` helpers directly and never fired `postHostAddAnnouncement` / `postHostRemoveAnnouncement` — so a character could join the chat with no Host message in the transcript (observed on Friday, chat `9de8d63d-895b-452c-a423-a087c842ae26`: Gary added at 21:38:15.701Z, only `[Chats v1] Chat updated` logged, no host-notifications activity). `processChatUpdates` now mirrors the POST handlers: the `addParticipant` branch resolves the just-added character via `repos.characters.findById(validatedData.addParticipant.characterId)` and posts the add announcement; the `removeParticipantId` branch resolves the participant's character name *before* the remove (since the row is gone afterward) and posts the remove announcement only when the character lookup succeeded. Status-change announcements via PUT were already covered because `handleParticipantUpdate` itself fires them regardless of which caller invokes it. (`app/api/v1/chats/[id]/helpers.ts`)
- **Chat streaming — `truncateToTokenLimit is not a function` no longer crashes turns when the previous-conversation summary is oversized**: `formatSummaryForContext` in `lib/chat/context/memory-injector.ts` used a lazy `require('@/lib/tokens/token-counter')` inside the truncation branch. In the Next.js webpack ESM dev bundle the dynamic `require` on a `@/`-aliased path didn't surface the module's named exports, so `truncateToTokenLimit` came back `undefined` and the `TypeError` propagated up through `buildContext` → `buildMessageContext` → `processMessage` (observed on Friday, chat `c4b7db4a-0b4a-4a68-b9ef-fee817dcd1f8`, at `TurnOrchestrator` chain depths 2 and 4 — only triggered when a chat had accumulated enough summary text to exceed the available summary budget, which is why it showed up mid-conversation rather than at startup). Replaced with a static top-of-file `import { estimateTokens, truncateToTokenLimit } from '@/lib/tokens/token-counter'`; no circular-dependency reason existed to defer the import. The other two `require('@/...')` callsites in the repo (`lib/database/backends/sqlite/backend.ts` for `startup-state` and `lib/startup/version-guard.ts` for `migrations/lib/database-utils`) are startup/migration boundary cases deliberately structured that way and remain untouched. (`lib/chat/context/memory-injector.ts`)
- **Folder rename — descendant folder rows now follow the parent**: `FoldersRepository.updatePathPrefix` (`lib/database/repositories/folders.repository.ts:293`), called by the `rename-folder` action in `app/api/v1/files/folders/route.ts:323`, used an anchored `^prefix` `$regex` to pick up descendant folder rows. The SQLite `$regex` translator (`lib/database/backends/sqlite/query-translator.ts`) cannot express anchored matches — it only rewrites `.*` → `%` / `.` → `_` and wraps the pattern in `%…%`, so the `^` and the `escapeRegex` backslashes passed through as literal LIKE characters and the query always matched zero rows. Net effect on the rename endpoint: the renamed folder's own row was updated (that edit goes through a direct `folders.update` on the resolved ID just above the `updatePathPrefix` call), and every file's `folderPath` was rewritten (the route does that itself via a `findByProjectId`/`findGeneralFiles` fetch + JS filter at lines 331–346), but the descendant *folder* rows were never touched — so the `folders` table accumulated stale paths pointing at the pre-rename tree even though the files underneath them had already moved. `updatePathPrefix` now fetches via `findAllInProject` and filters with `path.startsWith(oldPathPrefix)` in JS, mirroring the file-side code that already sat beside it. Two sibling methods on the same failure mode — `findDescendants` on folders and `findInFolderRecursive` on files — had no callers in the app but carried the same broken query; both are now rewritten to the same fetch-all + `startsWith` shape so they don't quietly match nothing if a future caller reaches for them. The query translator itself isn't touched; the earlier `$like` operator is reserved for the mount-index folder enumeration where it gets paired with `$in` for a meaningful SQL narrow. (`lib/database/repositories/folders.repository.ts`, `lib/database/repositories/files.repository.ts`)
- **Aurora / Scriptorium — vault-backed `Prompts/*.md` and `Scenarios/*.md` now actually load and rewrite**: The character-properties overlay's folder-listing query (`findManyByMountPointsInFolder` in `lib/database/repositories/doc-mount-documents.repository.ts`) used an anchored `$regex` pattern — `^Prompts/[^/]+\.md$` — against the SQLite backend. The translator's `$regex` case (`lib/database/backends/sqlite/query-translator.ts`) only rewrites `.*` → `%` and `.` → `_` and wraps the whole pattern in `%…%`, so regex anchors (`^`, `$`) and character classes (`[^/]+`) passed through as literal LIKE characters and the query matched nothing. Two downstream symptoms on vault-mode characters: (1) the read overlay reported `promptsFolderMountCount: 0` / `scenariosFolderMountCount: 0` in the logs and skipped the `systemPrompts` / `scenarios` overlay at `character-properties-overlay.ts:608`/`:638`, so character pages and new-chat prompt-picker menus kept showing the stale pre-vault DB column instead of the current vault files — on Friday, Amy's renamed "Free Agent" → "Amy" prompt was invisible; (2) `projectArrayIntoVaultFolder` (same file, line 1424) uses the same function to enumerate existing vault files before deciding what to delete, so the write path wrote new files but never deleted the old ones — the vault accumulated stale `.md` entries (Free Agent.md hung around next to Amy.md). The sync-back-from-vault action also reported `syncedSystemPromptCount: 0` for the same reason, so the DB column couldn't even be refreshed from a corrected vault. Fix adds a `$like` operator to the query translator that emits `LIKE ?` without the substring wrap (caller supplies wildcards; no regex rewriting), declared on `ComparisonCondition` and `ComparisonOperator` in `lib/database/interfaces.ts` — then rewires `findManyByMountPointsInFolder` to fetch with a prefix `$like: 'Prompts/%'` and narrow the result set in JS (`startsWith(prefix)`, top-level only via absence of `/` after the prefix, extension match). No other callers to change — the fix propagates automatically to the overlay read path, the sync-back action, and the write-path projection. Existing `$regex` usages (memories search, folders/files path-prefix lookups, chat message search) are untouched; each of those has its own semantics and a couple may have analogous bugs but are out of scope here. After the fix, the next write to a vault-mode character's prompts/scenarios will naturally re-project the folder and clean up any stragglers. (`lib/database/backends/sqlite/query-translator.ts`, `lib/database/interfaces.ts`, `lib/database/repositories/doc-mount-documents.repository.ts`)
- **Lantern and Aurora image announcements now quote the prompt they were aiming for**: The synthetic chat messages posted after a story-background or character-avatar regeneration used to say only "The Lantern has projected a new backdrop behind the proceedings" or "Aurora has refreshed the portrait filed under *X*'s name" — no indication of what the system was actually trying to produce, which left characters (and the human reader) guessing whether the new image matched intent. The image's generation prompt is already persisted on the `files` row (`generationPrompt` column, set by `lib/background-jobs/handlers/character-avatar.ts` and `lib/background-jobs/handlers/story-background.ts` at file-creation time), so `postLanternImageNotification` in `lib/services/lantern-notifications/writer.ts` now fetches the file by ID before composing the announcement and passes the prompt into `buildContent`. When present, avatar announcements read "*...aiming for: \"{prompt}\". The previous likeness is retired with due ceremony; the new one is attached here, should anyone care to take a fresh look.*" and background announcements read "*The Lantern has projected a new backdrop behind the proceedings, aiming for: \"{prompt}\". The resulting image hangs just above, attached for your perusal.*" When the prompt is missing (older files, rare race, or lookup failure) the message falls back to the original prompt-less wording — the fetch is wrapped in its own try/catch that logs at `debug` and never disturbs the announcement itself. The `character-image` kind (the `generate_image` tool path) is intentionally left alone: the requesting character already supplied the description explicitly in-chat, so repeating it back adds noise. Three new unit tests cover the new prompt-bearing and fallback shapes for both avatar and background kinds. (`lib/services/lantern-notifications/writer.ts`, `__tests__/unit/lantern-notifications-writer.test.ts`)
- **Document Mode — renaming the file in the editor title now actually renames the file, and the Librarian announces it in the chat**: `DocumentPane` at `app/salon/[id]/components/DocumentPane.tsx` has click-to-edit title logic that fires `onTitleChange(newTitle)` on Enter/blur, but the parent `app/salon/[id]/page.tsx` never passed that prop, so the `handleTitleSubmit` condition (`editTitle.trim() && editTitle !== document.displayTitle && onTitleChange`) short-circuited and the submit was a silent no-op. The input closed, the span re-rendered `document.displayTitle` from the unchanged prop, and the name "reset back to what it was" — same failure whether the active document lived in a filesystem-backed document store, a project, or a database-backed character vault. The backend had no endpoint to rename a Document Mode document either: `app/api/v1/chats/[id]/actions/documents.ts` carried `open`/`close`/`read`/`write`/`active`/`recent` but no rename action. New `rename-document` action takes a `newTitle` string, treats it as the new basename with the old directory preserved, appends the old extension if the user didn't supply one ("backstory" becomes "backstory.md"), rejects path separators and `..` segments, dispatches on `mountType` — `moveDatabaseDocument` from `lib/mount-index/database-store.ts` for database-backed stores, `fs.rename` for filesystem — refuses to overwrite an existing destination (409 for both backends, via `DatabaseStoreError.code === 'CONFLICT'` or a pre-`fs.rename` `fs.access` check), triggers a background re-index via `scheduleDocumentStoreRefresh` when a filesystem document-store file moves, and updates the `chat_documents` row's `filePath` + `displayTitle` so the UI and future opens see the new name. A matching Librarian announcement — fourth kind alongside `opened-by-user`, `opened-by-character`, and `saved` — is posted into the chat on success so characters present on the floor know the volume has been rechristened and the new path it answers to; `lib/services/librarian-notifications/writer.ts` gained `LibrarianRenameAnnouncement`, `buildRenameContent`, and `postLibrarianRenameAnnouncement` following the same never-propagate error semantics as the open/save writers. Client-side: a new `renameDocumentForChat` helper in `app/salon/[id]/hooks/documentModeApi.ts`, a `renameDocument` callback exposed by `useDocumentMode.ts` that flushes any pending autosave before calling the endpoint (so a rename doesn't lose an in-flight edit), patches `activeDocument.filePath` + `activeDocument.displayTitle` with the server response, and forwards the returned `librarianMessage` through the existing `onLibrarianMessageRef` path — the `mtime` carries through untouched because `moveDatabaseDocument` doesn't bump `lastModified` and `fs.rename` preserves filesystem mtime, so the next save's optimistic-concurrency check still matches. `page.tsx` now passes `onTitleChange={documentModeHook.renameDocument}` to `DocumentPane`. The `rename-document` action is registered in `CHAT_POST_ACTIONS` at `app/api/v1/chats/[id]/handlers/post.ts` and re-exported from `app/api/v1/chats/[id]/actions/index.ts`. (`app/api/v1/chats/[id]/actions/documents.ts`, `app/api/v1/chats/[id]/actions/index.ts`, `app/api/v1/chats/[id]/handlers/post.ts`, `app/salon/[id]/hooks/documentModeApi.ts`, `app/salon/[id]/hooks/useDocumentMode.ts`, `app/salon/[id]/page.tsx`, `lib/services/librarian-notifications/writer.ts`)
- **Agent mode — `submit_final_response` no longer ghost-wraps completed work from a previous turn**: Observed on Friday (chat `ea15913b-67a6-4ca6-8671-11ff6294d5b4`, 15:09–15:10): after a multi-turn agent run hit the 10-turn limit at 15:08:32 and produced a forced final response summarizing five file edits, the user sent a relational follow-up ("I love you, Amy…"). Amy re-entered agent mode, produced no conversational prose, and called `submit_final_response` on iteration 0 with a third-person recap of the *previous* turn's work — 965 reasoning tokens followed by a tool call whose `response` argument was the summary the user had already seen, with `content: ""` on the assistant message. The orchestrator's completion branch at `lib/services/chat-message/orchestrator.service.ts:1412` (`agentFinalResponse = args.response || currentResponse`) then overwrote whatever had streamed with that recap, so the user saw prose-shaped content briefly appear and get replaced by a meta-narration wrap-up. Two linked changes close the loop. (1) `buildAgentModeInstructions` in `lib/services/chat-message/agent-mode-resolver.service.ts` rewords the `submit_final_response` section to scope the tool explicitly to *this turn's* agentic work — "**Do NOT submit** if the user's message is conversational, relational, or a simple follow-up — just respond in character with natural prose" and "**Do NOT submit** just to re-summarize or wrap up work from a previous turn that already concluded." Memory search and other tools remain available on every turn; only the structured-summary framing is gated. (2) A belt-and-suspenders orchestrator guardrail that detects the ghost-wrap-up shape — `toolIterations === 0` AND `toolCalls.length === 1` AND `submit_final_response` is the lone call AND no prose content streamed — and, instead of taking the completion branch, synthesizes a `success: false` tool-result explaining why the call was rejected and instructing the model to respond conversationally (memory / other tools still allowed). The existing tool-loop plumbing then re-streams with that correction in context, so the next pass produces an in-character reply. `toolIterations` still increments, so the correction can't loop forever; if the model stubbornly calls `submit_final_response` again on iteration 1 without producing real work, that second call succeeds — at that point we stop second-guessing. Models that emit prose *alongside* a ghost `submit_final_response` slip through the guardrail intentionally (the prose check is the escape hatch; we don't want to discard real speech). `help/agent-mode.md` gained a "When It Fires — And When It Shouldn't" subsection explaining the new scope and the guardrail, and `ToolProcessingResult` was added to the types import in `orchestrator.service.ts` for the synthesized result. (`lib/services/chat-message/agent-mode-resolver.service.ts`, `lib/services/chat-message/orchestrator.service.ts`, `help/agent-mode.md`)
- **Background jobs — FAILED retries no longer strand forever when the processor auto-stops, and the Lantern routes around post-hoc image-moderation rejections through the Concierge**: Two linked bugs surfaced together on Friday (chat `af0642d1-c23a-4928-8184-4b33f4e2a6e7`, job `a9a56cbf-5661-446e-ad39-535f6cf1f212`). The user queued a story-background regeneration; Grok's image endpoint accepted the prompt but rejected the *generated image* post-hoc with `400 "Generated image rejected by content moderation."`. `markFailed` in `lib/database/repositories/background-jobs.repository.ts` correctly set `status='FAILED'` / `attempts=1/3` / `scheduledAt=2026-04-23T14:13:41Z` (60-second exponential-backoff retry), but two seconds later the processor's auto-stop path in `lib/background-jobs/processor.ts` fired — `claimNextJob()` returns only rows with `scheduledAt <= now`, which excluded the just-scheduled future retry, so the processor declared the queue empty, cleared the polling interval, and went quiet. Nothing else ever woke it back up: `ensureProcessorRunning` is only called from enqueue paths, so the retry sat idle indefinitely and the user's background regen never happened. Meanwhile the catch block at the image-generation call in `lib/background-jobs/handlers/story-background.ts` just re-threw the moderation error even though the Concierge already carried an `uncensoredImageProfileId` in `DangerousContentSettings` for exactly this case — the existing fallbacks for prompt crafting and appearance resolution checked it, but the generation call itself didn't. Three changes close both holes: (1) New `findNextScheduledAt()` on `BackgroundJobsRepository` — `$in: ['PENDING', 'FAILED']` + `$expr: { $lt: ['$attempts', '$maxAttempts'] }` sorted by `scheduledAt` ascending, limit 1 — returns the earliest future retry time across all retry-eligible jobs. (2) `processor.ts` gains a module-level `wakeUpTimer` with `armWakeUpTimer(scheduledAt)` (delay clamped to `[100ms, 5min]` so a far-future schedule doesn't pin a multi-hour timer and a past-due one gets a 100ms bounce) that `setTimeout`s a call to `ensureProcessorRunning()`. The auto-stop branch now queries `findNextScheduledAt()` before stopping and arms the timer if anything came back, so the FAILED job wakes the processor up exactly when its `scheduledAt` comes due. `startProcessor` and `stopProcessor` both call `clearWakeUpTimer()` so enqueues and shutdowns don't race a stale pending wake — explicit cleanup beats hoping nothing else starts the processor in the interim. (3) `story-background.ts` gains an `isImageModerationError(error)` helper matching the common phrasings (`"content moderation"`, `"content_policy"`, `"content policy"`, `"safety system"`, `"rejected by content"`, `"moderation_blocked"`) across Grok, OpenAI DALL-E, OpenRouter, and friends — keyword-based rather than status-code-based because every provider wraps its own error type and we don't want to care which SDK we caught. The catch block after `provider.generateImage` now checks moderation-shape + `dangerSettings.uncensoredImageProfileId` + "isn't the profile we just tried", and on match loads the uncensored profile, decrypts its API key through `connections.findApiKeyByIdAndUserId`, creates a second `createImageProvider` for its provider type, and retries with the same prompt/size/style. An `activeImageProfile` mutable tracks whichever profile ended up producing the final image, so the `generationModel` column on the resulting `files` row reflects reality (not the provider that rejected). The reroute logs both attempts through `logLLMCall` for Inspector visibility, and a reroute failure now throws `"Image generation failed after Concierge reroute: ..."` carrying the fallback's error message so the Inspector entry names the actual cause. Mirrors the existing prompt-crafting fallback at lines 430-468 and the appearance-resolution retry at lines 299-337 in the same file — same shape, same gating on presence of the uncensored profile rather than on `mode` (which already gates whether the Concierge is watching at all). Stranded jobs from before this fix will be picked up automatically on the next processor wake (which happens the moment any new job is enqueued, or on server restart). (`lib/database/repositories/background-jobs.repository.ts`, `lib/background-jobs/processor.ts`, `lib/background-jobs/handlers/story-background.ts`)

DELETE falls back to `deleteDatabaseDocument` from `lib/mount-index/database-store.ts` when the blob deletion misses, so the `doc_mount_documents` row, its `doc_mount_files` index mirror, and any `doc_mount_chunks` are all removed together and the store event fires. PATCH (description updates) is unchanged — documents don't have a description column, and a 404 there is the correct answer. (`app/api/v1/mount-points/[id]/blobs/[...path]/route.ts`)
- **Prospero — Files card count now tracks the linked Scriptorium store instead of the stale legacy files table**: `handleListFiles` in `app/api/v1/projects/[id]/actions/files.ts` backed `/api/v1/projects/{id}?action=list-files` with `repos.files.findAll()` filtered by `projectId`, so the number next to "Files" on the project page counted `files`-table rows — which Stage 1 never touched during migration, and which Stage 2 still writes alongside every mount-store upload. Net effect: after migration the count kept reporting pre-migration rows with stale on-disk storageKeys pointing at the archived `_doc_store_archive` directory, and if files were added to or removed from the project's store through the Scriptorium UI (outside the files-table write path) the count didn't budge. - **Prospero — "Browse All Files" now opens the project's own document store instead of a manually-linked one**: Stage 3 of the Scriptorium consolidation routed the Files card through the first database-backed store returned by `/api/v1/projects/{id}/mount-points`, which depended on whatever order `project_doc_mount_links.findByProjectId` happened to return — fine on projects with exactly one linked store but wrong on projects that also had a user-linked Scriptorium (e.g. a shared reference store). - **Physical backups — weekly, monthly, and yearly retention tiers now actually retain anything**: The tiered retention policy in `applyRetentionPolicy` (`lib/database/backends/sqlite/physical-backup.ts`) advertised "all for 7 days, weekly for 4 weeks, monthly for 12 months, yearly forever" and had code for every tier, but the weekly/monthly bucket loops iterated newest-first and `break`ed on the first match — so each bucket kept the *newest* backup in its age window. On the next day's retention pass, an even fresher backup entered the same window and became the new "kept" one; the previous day's pick was then missing from the `keep` set and got deleted at the bottom of the function. Net effect: nothing ever aged past ~8 days, so users who started the app daily ended up with ~7 daily + 1 "weekly" that was really just an 8-day-old daily. Weeks 2/3/4, month buckets, and the yearly tier never accumulated anything because no backup survived long enough to reach them. Phase 2 and Phase 3 now iterate oldest-first, keeping the *oldest* backup in each bucket — which has the most runway to age into the next tier on subsequent passes, instead of being aged out of its bucket and deleted the same day. A new regression test simulates 40 consecutive days of daily backup + retention runs with a stateful fs mock and asserts that all four weekly buckets plus the month-1 bucket end up populated; this would have failed loudly against the old code, which left only the 7-day daily window. (`lib/database/backends/sqlite/physical-backup.ts`, `__tests__/unit/lib/database/physical-backup.test.ts`)
- **Lantern — generated images are now delivered to each character exactly once**: The vision-content piggy-back added in `4c76a5af` (`buildMessageContext` in `lib/services/chat-message/context-builder.service.ts`) walked the last 6 ASSISTANT messages on every turn and re-attached every image file ID it found to that turn's request. Because the synthetic Lantern notification (story background, avatar regeneration, or `generate_image` tool result) sits in that window for many turns after it's posted, every character that took a turn while it was still in window saw the same image attached again, and again, and in multi-character chats the same image often went out 4–6 times in a row — observed as characters fixating on or repeatedly commenting on the same picture. The walk now stops at the requesting character's own most recent ASSISTANT message: in multi-character chats by `participantId` match (each character's responses are tagged), in single-character chats by the structural signal that character responses don't carry attachments while Lantern notifications always do. Anything older than the character's last turn was already delivered and is skipped. A new joining character with `hasHistoryAccess === false` clamps the walk further with a `historyCutoff = participant.createdAt`, so they never receive images that were posted before they joined the chat. The `ASSISTANT_IMAGE_LOOKBACK = 6` cap survives as a safety bound for first-turn responses in long chats. The renamed `collectLanternImageFileIdsForCharacter` helper is exported and covered by 11 new unit tests at `__tests__/unit/lib/services/chat-message/context-builder.service.test.ts` (own-turn stop, multi-character cross-talk, dedupe across messages, lookback cap, history cutoff, single-character attachment heuristic, ignored entry types). (`lib/services/chat-message/context-builder.service.ts`, `__tests__/unit/lib/services/chat-message/context-builder.service.test.ts`)
- **Salon/Aurora — Search & Replace modal no longer trips "Maximum update depth exceeded" on chats with frequent re-renders**: both call sites pass an inline object literal to `SearchReplaceModal`'s `initialScope` prop (`{ type: 'chat', chatId }` in `app/salon/[id]/components/ChatModals.tsx`, `{ type: 'character', characterId: id }` in `app/aurora/[id]/view/page.tsx`), so each parent render produced a fresh reference. Inside `useSearchReplace`, `reset` listed `initialScope` as a `useCallback` dependency, which meant a new `reset` identity per render; the close-modal `useEffect` in `SearchReplaceModal` then re-fired on every render and, while `!isOpen`, called `reset()` → `setScope(initialScope || null)` with the new object — a real state change that re-rendered the hook. With `ChatPage` re-rendering frequently during streaming, React's max-update-depth detector tripped. The hook now captures `initialScope` in a ref (kept current via a small `useEffect`) and `reset` is declared with empty deps, giving it a stable identity regardless of how callers spell their props. Both call sites are unchanged. (`components/tools/search-replace/hooks/useSearchReplace.ts`)
- **Prospero — Characters card no longer logs a React "unique key" warning when a project roster has duplicate IDs**: `app/prospero/[id]/components/CharactersCard.tsx` set `key={char.id}` on each grid card, which is correct in principle, but the underlying `project.characterRoster` is a `string[]` and, although every write path dedupes (`POST /api/v1/projects/[id]?action=add-to-roster`, the chat-creation helpers in `app/api/v1/chats/route.ts` and `app/api/v1/chats/[id]/helpers.ts`, and `ProjectsRepository.addCharacterToRoster`), older data on disk can still carry repeated IDs — the server enricher in `app/api/v1/projects/[id]/actions/project-crud.ts` then resolves the same `characterId` twice via `findById` and emits two roster entries with identical `id`s, which React correctly flags. `visibleCharacters`'s `useMemo` now threads a `Set<string>` through the filter, dropping any entry whose `id` is falsy or already seen, so the duplicates (and any freak nullish id) can't reach the grid. Quick-hide filtering is unchanged for the entries that survive the dedupe. (`app/prospero/[id]/components/CharactersCard.tsx`)
- **Wardrobe — `update_outfit_item` with `item_id: "none"` (or `"null"`/`""`) now clears the slot instead of throwing "not found"**: LLMs frequently fill required-looking string fields with the string `"none"` when they mean "no value" — so a call like `{slot: 'top', item_id: 'none'}` was taking the equip branch in `lib/tools/handlers/wardrobe-update-outfit-handler.ts`, doing `repos.wardrobe.findById('none')`, and failing with `WardrobeUpdateOutfitError: Wardrobe item not found with ID "none"` instead of clearing the slot. A new `normalizeNoItemSentinel` helper trims-and-lowercases `item_id` and `item_title` and maps `"none"`, `"null"`, and `""` to `undefined`, routing the call through the existing unequip branch (`unequipWithDisplacement` on the requested slot) — identical to the behavior when the field is omitted entirely. Real item IDs and titles (including any that happen to contain the substring "none") are unaffected because the match is full-string, case-insensitive, and post-trim. Fires a debug log noting the normalization when it happens. (`lib/tools/handlers/wardrobe-update-outfit-handler.ts`)
- **Server — transient LLM-provider network hiccups no longer crash the whole process**: Observed on Friday (2026-04-22 16:12:45 UTC): a successful multi-character turn on GROK finished, post-turn fan-out enqueued a burst of INTER_CHARACTER_MEMORY / MEMORY_EXTRACTION / CONVERSATION_RENDER jobs, an outbound fetch() to a Cloudflare-fronted provider (IP `2606:4700::6812:373`) got its socket cut mid-stream with undici's `TypeError: terminated` (cause: `SocketError: other side closed`, `UND_ERR_SOCKET`, 7173 bytes written / 1694 read), and ~2.5 minutes of log silence followed before `combined.log` shows `[JobQueue] Processor started` with fresh config and `Initializing MCP connection manager` — i.e. the dev server actually died and restarted. The smoking gun was `setupSQLiteShutdownHandlers` in `lib/database/backends/sqlite/client.ts`: its `process.on('unhandledRejection', ...)` handler closes the SQLite connection, releases the instance lock, and calls `process.exit(1)` *unconditionally* for any rejection — originally wired that way so a genuinely bad state wouldn't corrupt SQLite at shutdown, but the blast radius is every transient socket close from every outbound fetch to every LLM provider, image API, or MCP server, since any of those can leak a `terminated` rejection past a generator's `for await` boundary if the body consumer doesn't wrap it in try/catch. Fix: the `unhandledRejection` handler now classifies rejections. A new `isRecoverableNetworkRejection` helper matches against a `RECOVERABLE_NETWORK_CODES` set covering undici stream errors (`UND_ERR_SOCKET`, `UND_ERR_CLOSED`, `UND_ERR_ABORTED`, `UND_ERR_BODY_TIMEOUT`, `UND_ERR_HEADERS_TIMEOUT`, `UND_ERR_CONNECT_TIMEOUT`, both content-length-mismatch variants) and POSIX socket errors (`ECONNRESET`, `ECONNREFUSED`, `ECONNABORTED`, `EPIPE`, `ETIMEDOUT`, `EHOSTUNREACH`, `ENETUNREACH`, `ENOTFOUND`, `EAI_AGAIN`), walks both `error.code` and `error.cause.code` since undici's `TypeError: terminated` carries the interesting code on its `cause` not itself, and falls back to matching `reason.name === 'TypeError' && reason.message === 'terminated'` for older undici versions whose cause chain is missing. Matching rejections log at `warn` level with the error message, code, and cause code, and the process keeps running. Non-matching rejections hit the original exit path unchanged — the "something is genuinely wrong" case (type errors in repository code, assertion failures, etc.) still takes the server down cleanly rather than silently corrupting state. `uncaughtException` is untouched because sync throws past this point usually mean V8-level corruption, not a Cloudflare edge closing a socket. (`lib/database/backends/sqlite/client.ts`)
- **Wardrobe — gifts and edits now show up immediately on characters that read from the document vault**: The overlay that landed in `23557cc9` treats `wardrobe.json` as authoritative whenever a character has `readPropertiesFromDocumentStore` on and a linked mount point — `getOverlaidWardrobeItems` / `getOverlaidOutfitPresets` discard the DB loader's result entirely when the vault is valid. But every write path — the gift tool's `create_wardrobe_item`, the direct `POST /api/v1/characters/[id]/wardrobe`, and every preset mutation — only wrote to the DB via `repos.wardrobe.create` / `repos.outfitPresets.*`, so the new row became invisible on the next read (observed on Friday: a silk kimono gifted to Amy wrote `wardrobe_items` row `891c9418-…` at 15:07:12.682Z, and the refetch 62 ms later read the vault's pre-gift 7369-byte / 11-item snapshot and returned it verbatim). The one-time startup task `refreshVaultWardrobe` in `lib/startup/refresh-vault-wardrobe.ts` was the only thing that ever projected DB state into `wardrobe.json`, and it's gated by a `wardrobe_json_refreshed_v1` flag in `instance_settings` so it never fires twice on the same DB — meaning any drift that accumulated between startups was permanent until the flag was cleared by hand. Fix: a new `syncCharacterVaultWardrobe(characterId)` helper in `lib/database/repositories/character-properties-overlay.ts` reads the full DB state (`findByCharacterIdRaw` on both `wardrobe` and `outfitPresets`) and rewrites `wardrobe.json` via `writeDatabaseDocument`, no-oping for archetype rows (`characterId === null`) and non-overlay candidates. Writes are serialized per character via a `Map<string, Promise<void>>` chain so two concurrent syncs can't each read a stale DB snapshot and race-overwrite each other's result. Wired into `WardrobeRepository.create`/`update`/`archive`/`unarchive`/`delete` and `OutfitPresetsRepository.create`/`update`/`delete`/`removeItemFromPresets` — the last one collects the set of affected `characterId`s as it iterates and syncs each unique one once at the end, rather than one sync per modified preset. Vault-write failures log at `error` level but don't propagate: the DB write is already committed, and a thrown error would only tempt the caller into a retry that creates a duplicate DB row. To recover existing drifted vaults after upgrade, `DELETE FROM instance_settings WHERE key='wardrobe_json_refreshed_v1'` and restart — `refreshVaultWardrobe` then rewrites every linked character's `wardrobe.json` from the DB. The `quilltap db` CLI opens the DB read-only for one-shot SQL; use `--repl` mode (piping the DELETE via stdin works fine when the dev server isn't holding the write lock). (`lib/database/repositories/character-properties-overlay.ts`, `lib/database/repositories/wardrobe.repository.ts`, `lib/database/repositories/outfit-presets.repository.ts`)
- **New Chat form — Starting Scenario "Custom..." no longer hides the textarea on initial render**: In `components/new-chat/NewChatForm.tsx`, the Starting Scenario dropdown's `value` prop used `state.scenarioId ?? CUSTOM_SCENARIO_VALUE`, so both `null` and any unmatched id visually fell back to "Custom..." (the browser renders the first `<option>` when a controlled `<select>`'s value matches no option). But `showCustomTextarea` gated the textarea on a strict `state.scenarioId === null`. When `char.defaultScenarioId` pointed at a scenario that wasn't in the character's current `scenarios` array — stale default, deleted preset, or the modal's second effect leaking `char.defaultScenarioId ?? prev.scenarioId` across character switches in `components/new-chat/hooks/useNewChat.ts` — the dropdown visually showed "Custom..." but `showCustomTextarea` stayed `false`, so there was no textarea to type into below the dropdown and no preset card either (since `singleCharacterScenarios.find(s => s.id === stale)` returned `undefined`). Flipping to a real scenario and back worked because `handleScenarioSelectChange(CUSTOM)` explicitly sets `scenarioId: null`, at which point both conditions agreed again. Both conditions now derive from the same source of truth — whether a valid preset is actually selected: `showCustomTextarea = !singleCharacterScenarios || !selectedPreset` and `value={selectedPreset?.id ?? CUSTOM_SCENARIO_VALUE}`, so the dropdown's display and the textarea's visibility can't drift apart regardless of what stale id the scenarioId carries. (`components/new-chat/NewChatForm.tsx`)
- **Salon — "Maximum update depth exceeded" during SSE streaming, take three**: Follow-up to the `useOutfit` stable-deps fix in `23557cc9` and the `storyBackgroundsEnabled` fix in `b0e551ff`. The commit message on take two called out the *"three `setState`s per SSE chunk"* as the amplifier that lets any cascading dep-rotation tip React 19 past its update-depth tripwire. Resurfaced again in an eight-participant chain chat: the chain magnifies everything — every turn boundary whiplashes `setStreaming(false)` / `setWaitingForResponse(true)` in `onTurnStart` and the next content chunk flips them straight back — and a first attempt that only guarded those transition flags behind a `hasStartedStreaming` local (so they fire once per turn instead of once per chunk) still left `setStreamingContent` firing on every chunk, which tripped the same limit one line down. Two changes together: (1) the `hasStartedStreaming` flag stays (gates `setWaitingForResponse(false)` and `setStreaming(true)` to once per turn, reset on `turnStart`). (2) `setStreamingContent` is now rAF-coalesced: each chunk writes the accumulated content into a `streamingContentBufferRef` and schedules a `requestAnimationFrame` flush if one isn't already pending. The flush calls `setStreamingContent` at most once per animation frame, so the render rate is capped at the display refresh rate regardless of how fast chunks arrive — during a fast burst, 50 chunks in a frame collapse to a single state update. A new `resetStreamingContent` helper (replaces every `setStreamingContent('')` reset in the hook) cancels any pending rAF before clearing state, so a stale buffered flush can't stomp a reset at turn/chain/error/abort boundaries. A cleanup `useEffect` cancels the pending frame on unmount. End-to-end effect: in an eight-way chain where chunks can arrive faster than React can render them, the reconciler sees tens of state updates per second instead of hundreds, which gives any remaining effect-chain enough wall-clock time to unwind each render cycle before the next update lands. Doesn't paper over a genuine infinite loop if one still exists upstream, but widens the margin the same way takes one and two did — just at the volume knob instead of the dependency graph. (`app/salon/[id]/hooks/useSSEStreaming.ts`)
- **Salon — intermittent "Maximum update depth exceeded" during SSE streaming, take two**: Follow-up to the `storyBackgroundsEnabled` stable-deps fix in `b0e551ff`. The remaining cascade was in `app/salon/[id]/hooks/useOutfit.ts`: `fetchWardrobeForCharacter` listed `wardrobeCache` (React state) as its `useCallback` dep, so every `setWardrobeCache` call — one per character's wardrobe fetch — rotated the callback's identity, which rotated `refreshOutfit`'s identity, which rotated the mount effect inside `useOutfit` and the outfit effect at `page.tsx:398` depending on it. With three `setState`s firing per SSE chunk (`setWaitingForResponse(false)` / `setStreaming(true)` / `setStreamingContent(fullContent)` at `useSSEStreaming.ts:215`), any race where an outfit fetch completed mid-stream tipped the chain past React 19's update-depth tripwire — intermittent, because the cache stabilizes after the first fetch round and the loop only blew up when streaming started before the initial round settled. Fix: mirror the wardrobe cache into a `wardrobeCacheRef` and drop the state dep from `fetchWardrobeForCharacter`. The state copy still drives renders; the ref carries reads inside the callback so its identity is empty-deps stable. `refreshOutfit` consequently stabilizes too, so the outfit effect's `outfit.refreshOutfit` dep no longer shifts under streaming. (`app/salon/[id]/hooks/useOutfit.ts`)
- **Salon — wardrobe-change Notify button now inserts a `wardrobe`-fenced code block instead of roleplay-narration delimiters**: The "Notify" button that appears above the gutter tools when a character's outfit or wardrobe has changed (via the sidebar equip controls or a gift) previously wrapped the change description in the current roleplay template's narration delimiters (`*…*`, `[…]`, etc.) — which told the model to treat the change as narration prose rather than structured state. The handler in `app/salon/[id]/components/ChatComposer.tsx` now wraps the list in a triple-backtick fenced code block with `wardrobe` as the language tag, so the model sees the change as structured data. The `describeOutfit()` normalization in `lib/wardrobe/outfit-description.ts` is unchanged — empty slots still render as "naked", "topless", "bottomless", "barefoot", "no accessories", the fully-empty case still collapses to "completely naked and unadorned", and multi-slot items still group to a single line. One implementation detail worth flagging: the old path called `prependText`, which creates a single Lexical text node and then backslash-escapes any backticks when the editor serializes back to markdown — so the naive change produced a block starting with literal backslashed backticks in the sent message. The new code routes the combined markdown through `setMarkdown` instead, so the fence parses into a real `CodeNode` and survives serialization intact. The previously-threaded `narrationDelimiters` dependency was dropped from the insertion callback since it's no longer consulted there (it's still passed to `FormattingToolbar` for the unchanged roleplay-annotation buttons). (`app/salon/[id]/components/ChatComposer.tsx`)
- **Connection profile Auto-Configure now falls back across providers instead of dying when the default profile's provider is unavailable**: When the default connection profile's provider returned an error (observed on Friday: Anthropic 400 `invalid_request_error` — "You have reached your specified API usage limits. You will regain access on 2026-05-01 at 00:00 UTC."), `autoConfigureProfile` in `lib/services/auto-configure.service.ts` re-threw immediately and the route handler at `app/api/v1/connection-profiles/route.ts:567` masked the cause with a generic `"Failed to auto-configure profile"` — so the modal's toast said nothing actionable and the user had to log-dive to find the quota message. Two linked changes close the loop: (1) a new `pickAutoConfigureCandidates(allProfiles, defaultProfile)` helper builds an ordered list — default first, then for each *other* provider the highest-`modelClass` profile (Deep > Extended > Standard > Compact), skipping profiles with no `apiKeyId` unless they're OLLAMA. The per-profile analysis step (send-to-LLM + parse + cheap-LLM JSON cleanup) is now extracted into `analyzeWithProfile`, and the main loop iterates candidates sequentially, collecting `{ provider, modelName, error }` tuples on each failure and breaking on the first success. If every candidate fails, the thrown error now summarises every attempt (`"Auto-configure failed on all 4 candidate provider(s). ANTHROPIC (claude-sonnet-4-6): 400 ...; OPENAI (gpt-5-nano): ...; ..."`). Candidate list logs at debug and each attempt logs at info with `isDefault` + the chosen fallback provider if one succeeds. (2) `handleAutoConfigure` in the route now returns the underlying error message via `serverError(error.message)` instead of the hard-coded generic string, so the UI toast finally shows what actually went wrong. Grouping by provider (not cycling by tier) because quota/auth failures are per-provider — trying two Anthropic profiles when the first 429'd would just burn time. `cleanupWithCheapLLM`'s `defaultProfile` parameter was renamed to `currentProfile` since it's no longer guaranteed to be the default, and `getApiKey` now returns `''` for OLLAMA (no key needed) and includes the profile name in its "no API key" and "could not retrieve" errors. (`lib/services/auto-configure.service.ts`, `app/api/v1/connection-profiles/route.ts`)
- **OpenRouter plugin (1.0.33) — image attachments now reach vision-capable models instead of being silently dropped**: The previous per-profile `supportsImageUpload` flag (4.3-dev) opened the *upload-side* gate on OpenRouter profiles pointed at vision-capable models like `z-ai/glm-5v-turbo`, but the OpenRouter plugin itself still hardcoded `supportsFileAttachments = false` and its three send paths (`sendMessage`, `streamMessage` via SDK `callModel`, `streamWithTools` via direct fetch) all built request messages by mapping each `LLMMessage` to `{ role, content: m.content }` — never consulting `m.attachments[]`. End-to-end effect: with `supportsImageUpload=1`, the chat-attachment fallback at `lib/chat/file-attachment-fallback.ts` correctly *skipped* the cheap-LLM image-description summarizer (it thought the model would see the image natively), but the plugin then *also* skipped the image, so the model received the user's text-only message and behaved as if no attachment existed (observed in chat 58027ede on Friday: a user message announcing a Lantern photo plus an attachment row with file `48188506-...`, followed by an assistant turn that asked for the picture to be sent). Three changes to `plugins/dist/qtap-plugin-openrouter/provider.ts`: (1) new `buildMessageContent(m)` helper emits OpenAI Chat Completions vision content parts (`{ type: 'text', text }` + `{ type: 'image_url', image_url: { url } }`) when the message carries `image/{jpeg,png,gif,webp}` attachments — uses `attachment.url` if present, otherwise builds a `data:${mime};base64,${data}` URL — and falls back to the plain string when there are no images. (2) `streamMessage` now routes through the direct Chat Completions fetch path whenever the request has tools *or* image attachments; the SDK's `callModel`/OpenResponses input format (via `fromChatMessages`) doesn't round-trip `image_url` parts reliably, so multimodal traffic goes straight to OpenRouter's `/v1/chat/completions` endpoint where the OpenAI vision schema is the wire format.
