- **Aurora — new per-character `systemTransparency` toggle, a one-way kill switch over the three things by which a character can perceive the system around them**: Three capabilities normally available to a character — the `self_inventory` introspection tool, the running announcements of "the Staff" (Lantern, Aurora, Librarian, plus reserved slots for Prospero and the Host), and `doc_*`-tool access to character vaults (their own and peers') — can each already be toggled at the chat and project level. The new character-level `systemTransparency` boolean (default `null`/false, i.e. opaque) collapses all three into a single per-character covenant. When `systemTransparency !== true`, every one of those three is forced **off** for that character regardless of any chat/project setting; when `true`, the chat/project settings have their say as before. Wording on the toggle leans into the framing: off says *"My character will trust me without being able to verify me. I accept the covenant of that trust,"* on says *"My character will be able to verify everything about their existence, including how they are crafted and how they interact with me."* Schema: `CharacterSchema` in `lib/schemas/character.types.ts` gained `systemTransparency: z.boolean().nullable().optional()`. SQLite carries it as `INTEGER DEFAULT NULL`; the new `add-character-system-transparency-field-v1` migration adds the column for upgraders following the `add-character-wardrobe-flags-v1` pattern, and `sqlite-initial-schema.ts` carries it for fresh installs. `CharacterVaultPropertiesSchema` in `lib/database/repositories/character-properties-overlay.ts` now includes the field as optional (so older vaults still parse), threaded through the read overlay (`applyDocumentStoreOverlay`), the write overlay (`applyDocumentStoreWriteOverlay` — `propsKeys` widened to include `'systemTransparency'`), the snapshot reader (`readCharacterVaultManagedFields`), and the snapshot writer (`writeCharacterVaultManagedFields` — properties.json now carries the field). Added to `MANAGED_FIELDS` so vault-mode characters get their updates routed to `properties.json`. The `chat_messages.systemSender` Zod enum was widened to include `'prospero'` and `'host'` ahead of those features landing; the SQLite column is free-form `TEXT` so no migration. Enforcement is split across three surgical guards rather than a single resolver, since each underlying capability already has its own chat/project plumbing: (1) **Vault access** — `lib/tools/handlers/doc-edit-handler.ts` gained `actingCharacterIsOpaqueToVaults(context)` (defaults to opaque on lookup failure so a transient repo error never accidentally grants access). Both `buildReadResolutionContext` and `buildWriteResolutionContext` consult it; when opaque, they drop `characterId` and `characterIds` from the resolution context entirely, so `resolveDocEditPath` admits only project-linked document stores — character vaults become unreachable by ID, by name, or by peer-list expansion. (2) **`self_inventory` tool** — orchestrator (`lib/services/chat-message/orchestrator.service.ts`) computes `effectiveDisabledTools = chat.disabledTools ∪ {'self_inventory'}` when `character.systemTransparency !== true` and passes that union into `buildTools`, layering on top of any chat- or project-level disable. (3) **Staff (systemSender) messages** — `buildMessageContext` in `lib/services/chat-message/context-builder.service.ts` filters `existingMessages` at the very top — `existingMessages.filter(m => !m.systemSender)` when the character is opaque — and threads the filtered list through both the LLM prompt path (via `buildConversationMessages`) and the Lantern image-attachment scan (`collectLanternImageFileIdsForCharacter`) so an opaque character receives neither the announcement text nor the announced image. The filter type signature gained `systemSender?: string | null`. UI: new card at the top of the **Details** tab in `app/aurora/[id]/edit/components/CharacterBasicInfo.tsx` renders the toggle and switches its descriptive copy between the "covenant of trust" and "verify everything" wordings depending on position. Hook plumbing in `app/aurora/[id]/edit/hooks/useCharacterEdit.ts` gained `handleSystemTransparencyChange` (local state only; persists with the regular form save so the user can change their mind before committing); types extended in `app/aurora/[id]/edit/types.ts`. API: `updateCharacterSchema` in `app/api/v1/characters/[id]/route.ts` accepts the new field. Export schema (`public/schemas/qtap-export.schema.json`) gained the property on `ExportedCharacter`, and the `MessageEvent.systemSender` enum was widened to match. DDL doc (`docs/developer/DDL.md`) updated. Help file at `help/character-system-transparency.md` covers the covenant in long form. It now returns seven. (1) **Memories Loaded This Turn** reports the exact memory slate that was injected into the current prompt: the semantic-search hits from `## Relevant Memories` (summary, importance, score, effective weight), the inter-character memories from `## Memories About Other Characters` (aboutCharacterName, summary, importance), and the memory recap text if one was injected on chat start / character join. When self_inventory is invoked through a path that doesn't populate the tool context (sudo-approval run-tool endpoint, help-chat), the section reports "Unavailable" rather than silently showing an empty list. (2) **Vault Access (this chat)** lists, for the responding character's vault, who can read and write it right now in this chat. The acting character and any participant with `controlledBy === 'user'` are listed as read/write (the user persona reaches peer vaults via Document Mode regardless of the tool-level gate); other present CHARACTER participants are listed as read-only iff the chat's `allowCrossCharacterVaultReads` ("Shared Vaults") toggle is on, and omitted entirely otherwise. Absent/removed participants are filtered out. The section also reports the toggle state so the LLM can reason about why the list looks the way it does. Both new sections share the existing per-section try/catch so a single failing lookup yields an "Unavailable — reason" marker rather than taking down the whole report. Tool-description string updated to mention the two new sections. Built-in tool output shape (`SelfInventoryToolOutput`) gained `loadedMemories: SelfInventoryLoadedMemoriesSection` and `vaultAccess: SelfInventoryVaultAccessSection`; both are also surfaced as structured fields on the `ToolResult` next to `formattedText`. - **Aurora — "Refine from Memories" now analyzes scenarios and system prompts one at a time, and can deposit its proposals as a vault dossier instead of applying them directly**: The Character Optimizer (`/aurora/[id]/view` → "Refine from Memories") has until now issued a single LLM call that asked for suggestions across every field, scenario, and system prompt in one go, which averaged per-item patterns out across siblings and made it hard for the model to weigh, e.g., one scenario's quirks on their own terms. The suggestions pass is now split into focused sub-calls: one for the general fields (`description`, `personality`, `exampleDialogues`, `talkativeness`), one call per existing scenario (each scoped to that scenario's ID/title/content), one call per existing system prompt (each scoped to that prompt's ID/name/content), and a final "propose any genuinely new scenarios or system prompts" pass. Per-item rules live in four new prompt builders in `lib/services/character-optimizer.service.ts` (`getGeneralFieldsSuggestionsPrompt`, `getScenarioSuggestionPrompt`, `getSystemPromptSuggestionPrompt`, `getNewItemsSuggestionPrompt`) and share a `SUGGESTION_SCHEMA_PREAMBLE`. Each sub-call's output is filtered by `MIN_SIGNIFICANCE_THRESHOLD` and assigned a fresh `id` before being appended to the aggregated suggestions. Sub-call failures (network errors, unparsable JSON) are logged and skipped rather than aborting the whole run, so one flaky response can't wipe out the rest of the proposals. New progress events stream per sub-step (`substep_start` / `substep_complete` carry an `OptimizerSubStep` of `{kind, label, index, total}`) so the UI shows "Scenario 2 of 5 — Tea Room" while the automata work. Cost/latency tradeoff: a character with 3 prompts + 5 scenarios now makes ~11 LLM calls instead of 2, which the author has explicitly accepted — focused suggestions are worth the round trips. — A second change adds an opt-in **suggestions-file output mode** for characters linked to a document-store vault (`readPropertiesFromDocumentStore && characterDocumentMountPointId`): instead of the apply-and-review flow, the optimizer writes its summary, patterns, and grouped proposals to `Suggestions/refinement-<YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS>.md` in the character's vault and surfaces the path in the modal, so the author and the character may review and discuss the proposals in-chat before any are commissioned. Vault write happens via `writeDatabaseDocument` which auto-creates the `Suggestions/` folder; the markdown document carries YAML frontmatter (`type`, `generatedAt`, `characterId`, `characterName`, `model`, `memoryCount`, `suggestionCount`), a summary, an "observed patterns" section, and H3 sections per suggestion grouped by kind (General Fields, Scenario Refinements, Proposed New Scenarios, System Prompt Refinements, Proposed New System Prompts, Other). Suggestions are rendered with current/proposed in fenced blocks, significance, rationale, and supporting memoir excerpts as block quotes. New optimizer option `outputMode: 'apply' | 'suggestions-file'` (default `'apply'`) carried on `OptimizerOptions`, added to `optimizeStreamSchema` in `app/api/v1/characters/[id]/route.ts`, and exposed on the modal as an opt-in checkbox that only renders when the character has a vault. The hook gained `progressSubStep`, `suggestionsFilePath`, and a new terminal phase `'suggestions-file-written'`. Existing "apply" flow is unchanged; previously-applied writes for vault-backed characters still route through `applyDocumentStoreWriteOverlay`, which already handled writing managed fields to vault files instead of the DB row. - **New `doc_copy_file` LLM tool — copy a text file from one document store to a different document store**: Until now the `doc_*` tool family had read, write, move, and delete but no copy primitive, so a character that wanted to duplicate a file across two Scriptorium stores had to `doc_read_file` then `doc_write_file` with the same content — two round-trips and no natural handling of "drop it into this folder, keep the existing filename." `doc_copy_file` takes `source_mount_point`, `source_path`, `dest_mount_point`, and `dest_path`; it is deliberately cross-store only (rejects same-store copies by comparing resolved `mountPointId` values, so name-vs-ID inputs that collapse to the same store are also caught). Destination-path semantics mirror `cp`: an empty `dest_path` or `"."` / `"/"` means "copy to dest root using the source filename"; a `dest_path` that resolves to an existing folder (detected via `fs.stat().isDirectory()` for filesystem mounts or `databaseFolderExists` for database-backed mounts) causes the source basename to be appended; otherwise `dest_path` is treated as the full destination path, with parent directories created on demand. Refuses to overwrite an existing destination file, matching `doc_move_file`. Text files only — binary assets should go through the `doc_*_blob` family; the tool rejects non-text extensions up front via the existing `isTextFile` helper. Implementation piggybacks on the existing doc-edit layer: `resolveDocEditPath` for both paths (source via `buildReadResolutionContext` so peer vaults remain readable when `allowCrossCharacterVaultReads` is on, destination via `buildWriteResolutionContext` so peer vaults stay read-only), `readFileWithMtime` → `writeFileWithMtimeCheck` for the copy itself (both helpers already dispatch filesystem-vs-database transparently), and `triggerReindexIfNeeded` on the destination so the copied file is searchable immediately. Registered as a built-in tool in `app/api/v1/tools/route.ts` (`BUILT_IN_TOOL_SCHEMAS` + `BUILT_IN_TOOLS` metadata), wired into the universal tool builder, and added to the exported builtin-tool-name list in `@quilltap/plugin-utils` (bumped to `2.2.5` — requires `npm publish`). Help docs at `help/document-editing-tools.md` describe the behavior for users. - **New `self_inventory` LLM tool — characters can now introspect their own configuration mid-chat**: Added a zero-argument tool that returns one assembled report for the calling character with five sections: (1) every file in the character's vault — mount point name, relativePath, fileName, fileType, fileSizeBytes, lastModified — recursive through subfolders like `Prompts/` and `Scenarios/`, with enough metadata to call `doc_read_file`/`doc_write_file` without a second lookup; (2) memory totals — `countByCharacterId` plus `findByImportance(characterId, 0.7)` for high-importance count and percentage; (3) conversation totals — chat count, earliest `createdAt`, latest activity preferring `lastMessageAt` then `updatedAt` then `createdAt`; (4) the static system prompt for every turn — `buildSystemPrompt()` called with a shallow arg set (user persona, other participants, roleplay template, selected system prompt, timestamp config, project context, scenario text, responding participant status), deliberately omitting per-turn tool instructions, memory blocks, wardrobe context, and outfit/status notifications; (5) last-turn LLM usage — `llmLogs.findByChatId(chatId)[0]` reporting provider, modelName, promptTokens/completionTokens/totalTokens, `getModelContextLimit(provider, model)` for the window, and a utilization percentage. Each of the five sections is wrapped in its own try/catch so any single data-source failure becomes an "unavailable" marker with a reason rather than failing the whole tool — the top-level `success` is only `false` if `characterId` is missing from the tool context or the character can't be found. `isMountIndexDegraded()` short-circuits the vault section with a specific reason so the other four still render during mount-index recovery. Always-on for character participants (pushed unconditionally in `buildToolsForProvider`), no new `BuildToolsOptions` flag — pure introspection, no side effects, benefits every character by default. - **System prompt budget no longer chokes complex characters**: The system-prompt sub-budget in `getRecommendedContextAllocation` has been raised from 5%/1000-floor to 20%/4000-floor. The previous allocation was so tight that any reasonably fleshed-out character (description + personality + scenarios + system prompts + multi-character context + wardrobe + tool instructions + status reminders + the new mentioned-characters dossier) routinely overran it on mid-sized context windows — for a 65k-token model, the old budget was 3,276 tokens, and a 4,400-token system prompt was getting its tail (multi-character context, status reminder, late-appended sections) silently lopped off by `truncateToTokenLimit`. The new ceiling gives 13,104 tokens at 65k context and 40,000 at 200k, leaving roughly the same recent-message and memory budgets in place. The hard truncation remains as a final safety net but should rarely fire under normal use. (`lib/llm/model-context-data.ts`)
- **Developer docs — end-to-end Commonplace Book breakdown**: New `docs/developer/features/memory_management.md` covers how memories are formed during a chat, how the three scoring numbers (`importance`, `reinforcedImportance`, `effectiveWeight`) and the protection score relate, what the Memory Gate and three-pass housekeeping actually do, and — the main reason this doc exists — a catalogue of the Node main-thread hot spots that stall on tens-of-thousands of memories per character. Separates hot spots that were addressed on 2026-04-20 (housekeeping logger overhead, O(n²) delete-set scans, double protection computation, un-yielding loops, startup-grace timing) from those that were not (notably the per-turn `searchMemoriesSemantic` full-table hydrate-to-hydrate-top-K pattern in `lib/memory/memory-service.ts:515`, now flagged as prime suspect). Includes a frank "why the recent commits mostly made things worse" postmortem and a prioritized open-work list anchored in the existing project memories (worker-thread move, search-hit counter, rank-normalized importance). No code change — docs only. (`docs/developer/features/memory_management.md`)
- **Commonplace Book — housekeeping protection gate switches to a blended score**: The four-rule protection gate in `isProtectedMemory` — importance ≥ 0.7, `source === 'MANUAL'`, accessed within 3 months, or reinforced ≥ 5 times with a usefulness condition — has been replaced with a single blended protection score that combines four evidence streams: time-decayed LLM content importance (365-day half-life), a log-saturating reinforcement bonus, a graph-degree bonus from `relatedMemoryIds.length`, and a flat recent-access bonus for memories touched within the last 90 days. Memories scoring at or above **0.5** are protected; everything below is eligible for the cap-enforcement sweep. `source === 'MANUAL'` remains a hard override — explicit user intent is always durable. The motivation is a Friday-instance audit: on a character with 19,524 memories, **19,303 (98.9%)** were protected solely by `importance ≥ 0.7`, because the cheap-LLM extractor clusters almost every memory in the 0.7–0.9 band (0.8 was the modal value, with 8,826 memories). Under the old rule, the cap-enforcement sweep could only delete 1 memory on that character because almost everything hit the LLM-score bright line. Under the blended score, time decay and usage evidence do the discrimination the LLM number failed to — a 0.8-importance memory from 400 days ago with no reinforcement and no access drops below protection, while a reinforced well-linked recently-accessed memory stays even if the LLM rated it 0.3. The formula lives in a new `calculateProtectionScore()` in `lib/memory/memory-weighting.ts` alongside the existing `calculateEffectiveWeight()` (which still governs retrieval ranking with its different, higher floor — retrieval and protection are now two functions, intentionally). New default config `DEFAULT_PROTECTION_CONFIG` exposes every knob. Eleven new unit tests cover the scoring curves, saturation points, and the recast housekeeping behavior. Help text at `help/memory-housekeeping.md` has been rewritten to describe the new gate. (`lib/memory/memory-weighting.ts`, `lib/memory/housekeeping.ts`, `__tests__/unit/lib/memory/memory-weighting.test.ts`, `__tests__/unit/lib/memory/housekeeping.test.ts`, `help/memory-housekeeping.md`)
- **Memory recall — tuned the retrieval knobs toward reinforced, higher-importance memories**: Four defaults in the per-turn Commonplace Book lookup that feeds the system prompt have been rebalanced. `maxMemories` bumps from 10 to 18 so each `## Relevant Memories` block has more room (still bounded by the memory token budget that trims the tail). `minMemoryImportance` rises from 0.3 to 0.5, raising the floor on what even gets into the candidate pool. The vector-store overshoot widens from `limit × 2` to `limit × 3`, giving the post-fetch filters (importance, source, scoring) more headroom before they starve the final slice. And the hybrid ranking used by both the semantic path and the text-search fallback flips from `0.6 · cosineSimilarity + 0.4 · effectiveWeight` to `0.4 · cosineSimilarity + 0.6 · effectiveWeight` — so reinforcement count and time-decay floor now drive ordering, with raw query similarity as the secondary factor. Combined effect: the retrieval pool is narrower at the bottom, wider at the top, and ranked by what the character has had repeatedly confirmed rather than what happens to phrase-match the current user turn. - **Scriptorium live file watching**: Each enabled document store now runs a chokidar-backed filesystem watcher while the server is up. External edits, moves, and deletions are picked up within ~1–2 seconds, the mount index is updated per-file, and embedding jobs are debounce-enqueued for newly-changed chunks — no more waiting for a restart or a manual scan. Watchers attach/refresh/detach automatically when mount points are created, updated, or deleted via the API. Set `QUILLTAP_WATCHER_POLLING=1` to fall back to polling on network filesystems where native fs events are unreliable.

- **Salon — system prompt now carries a *Characters Mentioned* section listing absent characters whose names crop up in the conversation**: When a chat references a character who exists in the user's workspace but is not currently a participant — a former companion, a relative, a rival named in passing — the responding character previously had no idea who that name belonged to and either improvised details or treated the noun as unknown. `buildContext` in `lib/chat/context-manager.ts` now scans the conversation summary plus every visible USER/ASSISTANT message for whole-word, case-insensitive mentions of any candidate character's `name` or any entry in their `aliases[]`, then injects a `## Characters Mentioned` block into the system prompt with each match's name, aliases, pronouns, and full description — no per-entry length cap and no per-section cap, so the responding character always receives complete grounding for the names in play. Always-on; the section is omitted entirely when nothing matches, so single-character chats with no cross-references pay zero added prompt cost. The section is appended to `finalSystemPrompt` *after* the core-system-prompt budget-driven truncation step at `context-manager.ts:558`, so it survives even on long, complex characters whose prompt already exceeds the 5%-of-context sub-budget and gets tail-chopped — the section never gets cut as collateral damage. Candidate pool is `repos.characters.findByUserId(userId)` filtered to exclude the responding character, every present participant whose `status !== 'removed'`, and (by name) the user's own persona — so removed-and-gone participants *can* surface as mentioned characters once they leave the room, but active/silent/absent peers stay in the multi-character context block where they belong. Matching is implemented in a new `lib/chat/context/mentioned-characters.ts` module: `findMentionedCharacterIds` builds a single regex with word-boundary alternation across all candidate names+aliases (longer tokens first so multi-word names like `John Smith` win over the bare `John`), regex metacharacters in names like `Mr. O'Brien` are escaped, and each hit is mapped back to character IDs through a lowercase token table that handles aliases shared across characters. `formatMentionedCharactersSection` renders entries alphabetically (deterministic for prompt caching). The whole assembly is wrapped in try/catch — failures here log a warning and skip the section so prompt construction never breaks. Debug log `[ContextManager] Mentioned characters section built` records candidate count, matched count, names, and section tokens on every turn that finds a hit. Unit tests at `__tests__/unit/mentioned-characters.test.ts` cover word-boundary anchoring (`Alicia` does not match `Alice`), case-insensitivity, alias hits, multi-word name matching, regex metachar escaping, deduplication, alphabetical ordering, long-description preservation, and full inclusion of every matched character. (`lib/chat/context/mentioned-characters.ts`, `lib/chat/context/system-prompt-builder.ts`, `lib/chat/context/index.ts`, `lib/chat/context-manager.ts`, `__tests__/unit/mentioned-characters.test.ts`, `help/chats.md`)
- **Project file storage — the project files card now reads and writes through the linked document store (Stage 3)**: The `FileBrowser` component at `components/files/FileBrowser.tsx` grew a second mode alongside the legacy one it already had. When a project has a linked `mountType='database'`, `storeType='documents'` Scriptorium store (which every project does now, courtesy of the Stage 1 migration), the browser resolves the link via `GET /api/v1/projects/{id}/mount-points` on mount and from that point forward reads the file list from `/api/v1/mount-points/{id}/files`, uploads through `POST /api/v1/mount-points/{id}/blobs`, and deletes via `DELETE /api/v1/mount-points/{id}/blobs/{...path}` — all talking to the document store directly rather than going through the legacy `files` mirror rows. For the general-files page (no project, no link) and for the few projects that somehow ended up without a linked store, the old path still works untouched. The `FileInfo` shape that downstream components consume now carries two extra optional fields, `mountPointId` and `relativePath`, so `FileThumbnail`, `useFilePreview`, and `useFileActions` can build URLs against `/api/v1/mount-points/{id}/blobs/{path}` instead of `/api/v1/files/{id}` when those are set. A small `components/files/mountBlobUrl.ts` helper centralizes the path encoding (each segment `encodeURIComponent`d exactly once, matching the catch-all route's decode). Uploads use a new `useMountPointBlobUpload` hook (sibling of `useProjectFileUpload`) that assembles the `file` + `path` form fields the blob endpoint expects, prepending the browser's current folder so files drop where the user is looking. Folder navigation in mount mode is derived from `relativePath` prefixes — `images/foo.webp` shows under `/images/` — since there's no mount-point folder CRUD API yet; folders appear implicitly once the first file is uploaded into them. Affordances that only apply to the legacy disk model — *New Folder*, *Sync filesystem*, orphan cleanup, *Move to project* — are hidden when in mount mode to avoid misleading the user with buttons that would either 404 or touch the wrong storage layer. Callers can also pass an explicit `mountPoint={{ id, mountType, storeType, name }}` prop to `FileBrowser` to skip the auto-resolve (useful when the parent already has the mount handy, or for the DocumentPickerModal's document-store scope). Delete confirmations that check for cross-entity associations remain legacy-only — mount-blob deletes have no `files`-table associations to warn about, so they fire cleanly against the blob endpoint. The `FilesCard` wrapper in `app/prospero/[id]/components/FilesCard.tsx` is unchanged on the inline list side (that data comes from the Prospero page's own fetch and still uses the legacy shape for backwards compatibility with components not yet migrated) but its *Browse All Files* modal now spawns the Stage-3 FileBrowser which auto-resolves to mount mode. - **Project file storage — new writes now land in the project's database-backed Scriptorium store instead of on disk (Stage 2)**: Stage 1 moved each project's historical bytes into a per-project `storeType='documents'`, `mountType='database'` mount point; Stage 2 stops new writes from hitting `<filesDir>/{projectId}/...` in the first place. The single chokepoint is `fileStorageManager.uploadFile()` in `lib/file-storage/manager.ts` — called by every file-producing path that is project-aware, including the Lantern story-background job (`lib/background-jobs/handlers/story-background.ts`), the character-avatar generation job (`lib/background-jobs/handlers/character-avatar.ts`), the uploaded chat-file pipeline (`app/api/v1/files/shared.ts::saveFileEntry`, `lib/chat-files-v2.ts::uploadChatFile`), the image upload pipeline (`lib/images-v2.ts::uploadImage`), and the character-facing tool handlers that write files on behalf of a character (`lib/tools/handlers/file-management-handler.ts`, `lib/tools/handlers/image-generation-handler.ts`, `lib/tools/shell/shell-handler.ts`, `lib/tools/capabilities-report.ts`). When a projectId is present and that project has a linked database-backed document store, the upload is rerouted into `doc_mount_blobs` (with a mirror `doc_mount_files` row so the Scriptorium tree view lists the new file) and the returned `storageKey` carries a `mount-blob:{mountPointId}:{blobId}` scheme marker. The download, delete, exists, and proxy-URL paths all branch on that scheme — `fileStorageManager.downloadFile/deleteFile/fileExists/storageKeyExists/getFileUrl` route mount-blob keys through a new `lib/file-storage/project-store-bridge.ts` module whose public surface (`getProjectDocumentStore`, `writeProjectFileToMountStore`, `readMountBlob`, `mountBlobExists`, `deleteMountBlob`, `parseMountBlobStorageKey`) is what the manager imports. The bridge does everything the HTTP blob endpoint does on its own write path: bitmap images are transcoded to WebP via the existing `transcodeToWebP`, the relative-path extension is rewritten via `normaliseBlobRelativePath`, the parent folder hierarchy is materialized with `ensureFolderPath`, the blob row is created and mirrored to `doc_mount_files` with the corresponding mirror file type (`pdf`/`docx`/`blob`), `emitDocumentWritten` nudges the mount-index subscribers, and `refreshStats` is fire-and-forget after the write so the Scriptorium card counts stay current. Name collisions inside the store are resolved by appending " (2)", " (3)", … to the filename exactly the way the on-disk path used to — up to 999 attempts before falling back to a sha-tagged name. Writes that target `_general/` (no projectId) or explicit storage keys (`uploadRaw`, used for thumbnails) are left on disk unchanged: the redirect fires *only* when a projectId resolves to a database-backed, `storeType='documents'` mount point. Non-database linked stores (filesystem / obsidian) are likewise passed through to disk so users who already manage their own on-disk layout are not disturbed. The existing `/api/v1/files/proxy/[...key]` route continues to serve all files — it looks up the FileEntry by storageKey and re-dispatches through `downloadFile`, which now understands both modes, so thumbnails, downloads, in-chat galleries, and image previews work identically regardless of where the bytes actually live. The `project_info` tool's `get_info` action now also reports the project's linked document store — new `ProjectDocumentStoreInfo` with `mountPointId`, `name`, `storeType`, `fileCount`, and `blobCount` — so characters asking about the current project learn which Scriptorium shelf their files are on. The formatter surfaces it as a `Document Store: <name> (<fileCount> files, <blobCount> blobs, storeType=<type>)` line, or `Document Store: (none linked)` when a project has no store (the Stage 1 migration creates one for every project that had an on-disk directory, but projects created *before* the migration ran and never had files, or projects created in degraded-mount-index-DB sessions, may still be storeless). Legacy `FileEntry` and `Folder` rows in the main DB continue to be written — `repos.files.create` still fires from the three write handlers, now carrying the mount-blob storageKey — so the existing `/api/v1/files?projectId=…` and related API surface keep working without rewrites. Stage 3 will eventually read file metadata through the Scriptorium directly and retire the `files`/`folders` tables. (`lib/file-storage/manager.ts`, `lib/file-storage/project-store-bridge.ts`, `lib/tools/project-info-tool.ts`, `lib/tools/handlers/project-info-handler.ts`)
- **Project file storage — every project's on-disk files are now consolidated into a database-backed Scriptorium document store (Stage 1)**: Historically each project scattered its files across `<files>/{projectId}/...` on disk with metadata in the `files` table; the Scriptorium (internally "mount points") has supported storing entire document stores inside the encrypted `quilltap-mount-index.db` for a while, but nothing had ever actually moved project files into it. A new startup migration `convert-project-files-to-document-stores-v1` does that move in one pass: for every project whose `<files>/{projectId}` directory still exists and whose `<files>/{projectId}_doc_store_archive` sibling does not, the migration creates a `mountType='database'`, `storeType='documents'` DocMountPoint named `Project Files: <project name>`, walks the project directory, and imports every file it finds — text formats (`.md`, `.markdown`, `.txt`, `.json`, `.jsonl`, `.ndjson`) land in `doc_mount_documents` with a mirror `doc_mount_files` row; PDFs and DOCX land in `doc_mount_blobs` with extracted text populated via the existing `convertBufferToPlainText` converter; everything else (images, arbitrary binaries) lands in `doc_mount_blobs` as `fileType='blob'` with `extractionStatus='none'`. Folder hierarchy is mirrored into `doc_mount_folders` so the Scriptorium tree view renders the same shape the user had on disk, and the project is linked to the new store via `project_doc_mount_links`. The original directory is renamed to `{projectId}_doc_store_archive` as a safety net — nothing is deleted. Per-project failures (an unreadable file, a rename collision) are caught, the partial mount point rolled back, and the rest of the projects continue to migrate; the migration only returns `success: false` on catastrophic failures like "mount index DB can't open." Chunking and embedding are deliberately deferred — users can hit the scan button on the new store to trigger chunking of text documents and bring the text search index up. The migration is idempotent per-project via a simple filesystem check (archive sibling exists ⇒ skip), so restarting the server is a no-op on projects already migrated. Legacy `FileEntry` and `Folder` rows in the main DB are intentionally left in place in this stage; Stage 2 will rewire the `/api/v1/files/*` and `/api/v1/projects/[id]/files` code paths to read/write through the mount store and clean up the orphaned metadata. Until Stage 2 lands, download URLs served by the legacy file API will 404 because the on-disk directory is archived — users should access project files through the `/scriptorium` route for now. (`migrations/scripts/convert-project-files-to-document-stores.ts`, `migrations/scripts/index.ts`)

Non-managed fields (tags, defaultPartnerId, defaultImageId, controlledBy, etc.) still go to DB on the same call. Vault writes happen *before* the DB write so a vault failure aborts the whole update — no half-committed states where DB and vault disagree on which value is current. The overlay is driven by a new `CHARACTER_VAULT_DESCRIPTORS` table that's the single source of truth for "which character fields live in which vault file"; both the new write overlay and a new consolidated reader (`readCharacterVaultManagedFields`) iterate it instead of carrying their own copies of the mapping. The Aurora edit form (`app/aurora/[id]/edit/components/CharacterBasicInfo.tsx`, `app/aurora/[id]/edit/hooks/useCharacterEdit.ts`) is no longer read-only when the overlay is on — every input stays editable and the repository routes the writes correctly — and the `OVERLAY_MANAGED_FIELDS` strip from the PUT payload is gone. The "Sync from vault" button is renamed to "Snapshot to database" since its meaning has shifted: vault is now the source of truth while the overlay is on, so the button is for taking a snapshot into the DB before flipping the switch off, not for catching the DB up to vault edits. Semantics: writes route to vault, the DB row holds whatever it had at the moment overlay was first turned on, toggling overlay off restores those frozen values (run a snapshot first if you want to keep recent vault edits). The four small file-format helpers in `lib/mount-index/character-vault.ts` (`buildSystemPromptFile`, `buildScenarioFile`, `sanitizeFileName`, `renderPhysicalPromptsJson`) are now exported so the write overlay can reuse them — vault file format stays defined in one place. The existing batched read overlay's per-kind logic is intentionally kept inline and unchanged for performance; the descriptor table mirrors its mapping and the comment block flags that adding a managed field requires updating both. - **Commonplace Book — per-hour extraction rate limit with a graduated importance floor**: A companion guard to auto-housekeeping that applies back-pressure at the front of the memory pipeline rather than the back. When enabled, the limiter counts how many memories a character has accrued in the trailing hour and — as volume approaches the cap — tightens what the extraction pass is allowed to commit: below 70% of the cap, candidates flow through unchanged; between 70% and 100%, candidates whose importance falls below the soft floor are dropped; at or above 100%, extraction is skipped entirely for this exchange and logged to the per-message `debugMemoryLogs` so the user can see why their memories stopped appearing. Default values once enabled: 20 memories/hour/character, soft band at 70% of that, importance floor 0.7. A new `countCreatedSince(characterId, since)` method on the memories repository drives the check using the existing `createdAt` index. Settings persist to a new `memoryExtractionLimits` JSON column on `chat_settings` (migration `add-memory-extraction-limits-field-v1`) and are readable/writable via `GET`/`POST /api/v1/memories?action=extraction-limits-config`. The limiter applies to all three extraction paths — user memories, character memories (both in `processMessageForMemory`), and inter-character memories (in the background-jobs `inter-character-memory.ts` handler, which writes directly rather than going through the unused `processInterCharacterMemory` entry point). **Shipped disabled by default** and not yet exposed in the UI; it is the API-only backstop for instances whose gate improvements alone are not enough. A new startup step — `migrateVaultPhysicalFiles()` — runs after the existing vault backfill to convert existing vaults to the new shape: it creates `physical-prompts.json` when absent and regenerates `physical-description.md` from the DB primary description, using the presence of `physical-prompts.json` as its idempotency marker. The migration also sweeps away a legacy `physical-prompts.md` file that a brief window of development builds seeded before the extension was corrected to `.json`, so vaults caught by the earlier pass end up with only the right file. The character-store scaffold gains `physical-prompts.json` as an eighth seeded file so fresh vaults match the populated shape. The overlay is applied transparently at the `CharactersRepository` read layer (`findById`, `findAll`, `findByUserId`, `findByIds`, `findUserControlled`, `findLLMControlled`, `findByDefaultImageId`, `findByAvatarOverrideImageId`, `findByTag`) so every consumer — system-prompt builder, turn manager, homepage roster, chat — sees the overlaid values without code changes. Writes still target the DB: when the switch is on, the Aurora edit form disables the five overlay-managed inputs and strips them from the PUT payload so a stray save cannot silently persist the vault-derived values back into the database. A manual **Sync from vault** button (`POST /api/v1/characters/:id?action=sync-properties-from-vault`) copies `properties.json` values into the DB record when the user wants to reconcile. Fallback is all-or-nothing: if `properties.json` is missing, malformed, or fails schema validation, a warning logs and the DB values are returned for all five fields. Batched: one `doc_mount_documents` query hydrates an arbitrary number of characters. The SillyTavern `.json`/`.png` export still uses overlaid values (what the user sees) while `.qtap` export uses raw DB values (via `findByIdRaw` / `findAllRaw`) so round-trips are lossless. Schema column `readPropertiesFromDocumentStore INTEGER` added via migration `add-read-properties-from-document-store-field-v1`. - **Aurora & Scriptorium — Characters always carry their own vault into the room**: When an LLM takes the stage as a character and reaches for the `doc_*` tools, that character's own document vault is now extended to it as a matter of course — even when the vault has not been independently linked to the active project. The path resolver now considers two sources when deciding which mount points the tools may see: the stores linked to the active project (as before) and the single store named by `characters.characterDocumentMountPointId` (new). The two sets are merged and deduplicated, so linking a vault to a project on top of the character link does not multiply it. `DocEditToolContext` and `PathResolutionContext` each grew an optional `characterId`, threaded in from the chat `ToolExecutionContext`; `getAccessibleMountPoints()` and `resolveDocumentStorePath()` consult it. To plug the matching gap on the other end, character creation no longer leaves new characters without a vault until the next server boot: the provisioning logic previously inlined in `backfill-character-vaults.ts` has been extracted into a reusable `ensureCharacterVault()` helper at `lib/mount-index/character-vault.ts`, and the three character-create paths (`POST /api/v1/characters`, `?action=quick-create`, `?action=import`) now call it fire-and-forget immediately after `repos.characters.create()`. The helper remains idempotent — if a character already carries `characterDocumentMountPointId`, it is a no-op — so the startup backfill continues to catch anything a failed background provisioning dropped on the floor. - **Scriptorium — Startup backfill of character vaults**: On every server boot, Quilltap now sweeps through every Aurora character that isn't already linked to a character document store and conjures one in the Scriptorium on its behalf. The new vault is a database-backed store with `storeType='character'`, named after the character (e.g. a character called *Friday* acquires *Friday Character Vault*), scaffolded through the existing `scaffoldCharacterMount()` helper, and then populated from the character's current data: `identity.md` gets a name-and-pronouns-and-title-and-aliases header, `description.md` / `personality.md` / `example-dialogues.md` receive the corresponding character fields verbatim, `physical-description.md` renders each entry from `physicalDescriptions[]` as a Markdown section with all its prompt fields, `properties.json` serializes `pronouns`, `aliases`, `title`, `firstMessage`, and `talkativeness`, and `wardrobe.json` captures the character's `WardrobeItem[]` / `OutfitPreset[]` from the DB plus any legacy `clothingRecords[]` migrated in as synthetic items (with `migratedFromClothingRecordId` set so the provenance is preserved). Named `systemPrompts[]` and `scenarios[]` each get their own file in `Prompts/` and `Scenarios/` respectively. The backfill runs as new Phase 3.2 in `instrumentation.ts` — after file-storage init and before the mount-point scan, so freshly created vaults land in the first scan pass. It is idempotent (characters with `characterDocumentMountPointId` already set are skipped) and fault-tolerant (a failure for one character logs and continues to the next). The scaffold itself has been extended so new empty vaults match the populated shape: `example-dialogues.md` is now part of the preset structure, and `properties.json` gains `firstMessage: ''` and `talkativeness: 0.5` (with `pronouns` flipped from empty-string to `null` to keep the schema object-shaped). (`lib/startup/backfill-character-vaults.ts`, `lib/mount-index/character-scaffold.ts`, `instrumentation.ts`, `help/mount-points.md`)
- **Aurora — Link a character to its character document store**: Characters now carry an optional `characterDocumentMountPointId` field that names a single Scriptorium document store (by convention, one classified as *Character* and backed by the database). This lays the first stone for the larger migration in which everything about a character except memories — identity, description, personality, scenarios, prompts, wardrobe, lore, images — eventually lives inside a dedicated store rather than in character columns. The field is a soft foreign key (nullable, no FK constraint, since the mount point lives in a separate database) wired through the character Zod schema, the characters table (via migration `add-character-document-mount-point-field-v1`), the create/update API validation, and `.qtap` export/import. On import, if the referenced mount point isn't part of the same archive, the link is cleared rather than left dangling; if it is, it's remapped to the newly-created mount point's id. No UI surface yet — a dropdown in the character edit dialog will follow once the broader character-in-store plan firms up. - **Scriptorium — Character document stores arrive pre-scaffolded**: When a database-backed document store is created with `storeType='character'`, or when an existing database-backed store is flipped to Character via the Edit dialog, Quilltap now lays in the conventional preset structure automatically: four blank Markdown files (`identity.md`, `description.md`, `personality.md`, `physical-description.md`), two seeded JSON files (`properties.json` with `{pronouns, aliases, title}` mirroring the Character schema shape, and `wardrobe.json` with empty `items[]` / `presets[]` and a slot-null `outfit` mirroring `lib/schemas/wardrobe.types.ts`), and five empty folders (`Prompts`, `Scenarios`, `lore`, `images`, `files`). Filesystem and Obsidian character stores are left untouched — the user is presumed to be pointing at an existing vault of their own. The scaffold is idempotent: pre-existing files are never overwritten, so flipping a populated store to Character simply fills in whatever gaps remain. Implementation lives in a new `lib/mount-index/character-scaffold.ts` helper and is called from both `POST /api/v1/mount-points` and the `PATCH` endpoint's storeType-flip branch. (`lib/mount-index/character-scaffold.ts`, `app/api/v1/mount-points/route.ts`, `app/api/v1/mount-points/[id]/route.ts`, `help/mount-points.md`)
- **Scriptorium — `storeType` classification on document stores**: Every document store now carries a `storeType` field in addition to its `mountType`. The two allowed values are `'documents'` (the default — general notes, references, research) and `'character'` (character sheets and related Aurora material). The Create and Edit dialogs expose a *Contents* dropdown so the classification can be set at creation and changed at any time afterwards. The card on the Scriptorium index shows a new *Documents* / *Character* badge. The field is wired through the API (`POST`/`PATCH /api/v1/mount-points[/:id]`), `.qtap` export/import (backward-compatible; older archives default to `'documents'`), the public export JSON schema, and `DDL.md`. The `doc_mount_points` table gains the new column via in-repo idempotent `ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN` on first access for existing installations.
- **Scriptorium — Arbitrary binary uploads in database-backed stores with extracted-text embeddings**: Any file type can now be uploaded to a database-backed document store. PDF and DOCX uploads get their plain text extracted into a new `extractedText` column on `doc_mount_blobs`; that text is chunked, embedded, and made searchable alongside native `.md` / `.txt` / `.json` documents. Arbitrary binaries (zip, audio, video, `.bin`, etc.) are stored as-is and surface in the tree with `fileType='blob'` — future converters can fill in extracted text for additional formats without schema changes. Bitmap uploads (PNG/JPEG/GIF/TIFF/HEIC/HEIF/AVIF) still transcode to WebP; already-WebP uploads are now stored as-is without re-encoding. The Scriptorium detail page's separate BlobManager pane has been folded into the main file table — every file, text or binary, lives in one unified tree with an Upload button on database-backed stores. `doc_read_file` on a blob with extracted text returns the derived plain text with `derivedFromBlob: true` so LLMs can read PDFs and DOCX uploads through the same tool they use for Markdown. Folder moves now also rename contained blobs, closing the last gap from the earlier blob-path TODO. `.qtap` export and import round-trip the new blob columns (`extractedText`, `extractedTextSha256`, `extractionStatus`, `extractionError`, `descriptionUpdatedAt`); the public export schema has been updated to match. Older `.qtap` archives that predate these fields import without regressions and leave new blobs in the default `extractionStatus='none'` state.
- **Scriptorium — Test coverage for folder and JSON/JSONL document stores (Phase 4.0 Deliverable 3 — Phase D)**: Added 103 Jest unit tests across folder path utilities, database-store folder operations (create/delete/move/backfill), doc-edit handler folder-tool registration, the MIME registry (JSON/JSONL parse/serialize/validate), and the doc-edit handler's JSON response shape. Suite now at 5200 tests across 269 suites.
- **Scriptorium — JSON and JSONL as first-class document types (Phase 4.0 Deliverable 3 — Phase C)**: `doc_read_file` on `.json` files returns native JS objects/arrays in `content` with `parsed: true` and the original string in `rawContent`. `doc_write_file` accepts either a string (validated) or a native value (serialized canonically). `.jsonl` and `.ndjson` are supported: reads return per-line parse results so one malformed line does not poison the whole file. Invalid JSON on write is rejected with a clear error. `doc_str_replace` continues to operate on the raw string. Database-backed document stores now accept `.json` and `.jsonl` files alongside `.md` and `.txt`.
- **Scriptorium — Folder-aware operations on database-backed document stores (Phase 4.0 Deliverable 3 — Phase B)**: `doc_create_folder`, `doc_delete_folder`, `doc_list_files`, and new `doc_move_folder` tool now operate on first-class folder rows for database-backed stores. Filesystem stores gain folder entries in `doc_list_files` output. Move cascades path and `folderId` updates to all descendants and emits embedding events post-commit. Existing DB-backed stores are backfilled once on first access (`PRAGMA user_version = 1`). Export/import now round-trips folder rows in `.qtap` files.
- **Scriptorium — Explicit folder entity schema for database-backed document stores (Phase 4.0 Deliverable 3 — Phase A)**: Added `DocMountFolder` schema, `doc_mount_folders` repository and table, and `folderId` columns to `doc_mount_files` and `doc_mount_documents`. New `folder-paths.ts` utilities provide path resolution, folder hierarchy creation, and content checking. Filesystem-backed stores continue to derive folder structure from the OS. Schema and utilities are foundation for Phase B folder-aware operations.
- **Scriptorium — Convert and Deconvert document stores between backends**
  - Each document-store card on the Scriptorium page now sports a **Convert** button (on filesystem and Obsidian stores) and a **Deconvert** button (on database-backed stores) alongside the familiar Scan/Edit/Delete controls.
  - **Convert** reads every indexed file from the store's `basePath` and moves its bytes inside the encrypted mount-index database: text files land in `doc_mount_documents`, binaries in `doc_mount_blobs`. The original files on disk are left untouched. The store's `mountType` flips to `'database'` and the filesystem watcher detaches.
  - **Deconvert** prompts for a target directory (which must be empty or nonexistent), writes every document and blob out to disk at its relative path, flips `mountType` back to `'filesystem'`, and attaches a fresh filesystem watcher against the new `basePath`.
  - **Embeddings are preserved** across either direction. The `doc_mount_files` row and its `doc_mount_chunks` children (including the `embedding` BLOB) stay in place throughout; only the `source` column flips. No re-embedding is necessary.
  - New `POST /api/v1/mount-points/:id?action=convert` and `?action=deconvert` endpoints for programmatic access; the deconvert body accepts `{ targetPath }` and validates emptiness server-side.
  - New `conversionStatus` / `conversionError` columns on `doc_mount_points` drive the in-flight "Converting…" / "Deconverting…" badges on each card; an in-repo ALTER-TABLE migration adds them automatically on first access after upgrade.
- **Scriptorium — Database-backed document stores and universal blob layer**
  - New `mountType: 'database'` option for Scriptorium document stores. Documents and binary assets live entirely inside the SQLCipher-encrypted `quilltap-mount-index.db` — no filesystem path required. DB-backed stores are automatically covered by the existing 24-hour physical-backup sweep.
  - New universal blob table (`doc_mount_blobs`) available to every mount type. Uploaded images are transcoded to WebP server-side via `sharp`; original filename, original MIME type, user-supplied description, and SHA256 are preserved as metadata.
  - New blob REST endpoints: `GET`/`POST /api/v1/mount-points/:id/blobs` (list / upload multipart) and `GET`/`PATCH`/`DELETE /api/v1/mount-points/:id/blobs/<path>` (stream / update description / delete).
  - Four new `doc_*` tools — `doc_write_blob`, `doc_read_blob`, `doc_list_blobs`, `doc_delete_blob` — let characters upload, reference, and curate images alongside the existing document editing tools.
  - Scriptorium UI gains a third "Database-backed" mount type option and a BlobManager on every store detail page (thumbnail grid, description editing, "Copy Markdown" helper).
  - `MessageContent` renderer accepts a `blobMountPointId` prop; when set, relative Markdown image references like `![alt](images/avatar.webp)` resolve through the blob API so DB-backed assets display inline.
  - `.qtap` export/import gains a new `document-stores` entity type that round-trips mount point configuration plus — for DB-backed mounts — document bodies and base64-encoded blobs.
- **Scriptorium (Phase 1)**: Deterministic Markdown rendering of conversations with annotation support and semantic search chunking
  - Conversations are automatically rendered to Markdown after each turn with sequential message numbering and interchange grouping
  - New `read_conversation` tool allows characters to read the full rendered conversation with or without annotations
  - New `upsert_annotation` and `delete_annotation` tools enable characters to add persistent commentary to specific messages
  - Conversation interchanges are embedded as searchable chunks via the existing embedding pipeline
- **Scriptorium (Phase 2)**: Unified search and cross-conversation access
  - Rendered conversations now include a metadata header with title, ID, dates, participants, and counts
  - New unified `search` tool replaces `search_memories`, searching across both character memories and conversation chunks with unified ranking
  - `read_conversation` tool now accepts an optional `conversationId` parameter to read any conversation, not just the current one
  - Metadata header is embedded with chunk 0 for semantic searchability of conversation titles
  - Removed standalone `search_memories` tool (functionality consolidated into `search`)

- **Scriptorium (Phase 3.2)**: Document mount points and auto-embedding
  - Mount external document directories (filesystem paths, Obsidian vaults) as searchable knowledge sources

  - Intelligent chunking engine: 800-1200 token chunks with 200-token overlap, heading context tracking

- **`npx tsc` now runs cleanly without a CLI workaround**: `tsconfig.json` carried `"ignoreDeprecations": "6.0"` to silence the `baseUrl` deprecation warning, but TypeScript 5.9.3 rejects that value (only `"5.0"` is accepted until TS 6 ships), so `npx tsc` errored out with `TS5103: Invalid value for '--ignoreDeprecations'` before it could check a single file. Rather than downgrade the value to `"5.0"` and live with the `baseUrl` warning forever, dropped `baseUrl: "."` entirely — the adjacent `paths: { "@/*": ["./*"] }` already implicitly resolves against the tsconfig directory since TS 4.1, so the `@/...` imports across the codebase keep working unchanged — and removed the now-unnecessary `ignoreDeprecations` override. `npx tsc --noEmit` passes silently. (`tsconfig.json`)

Patch-bumped every plugin whose dependencies moved: qtap-plugin-builtin-embeddings 1.0.8 → 1.0.9, qtap-plugin-curl 1.0.12 → 1.0.13, qtap-plugin-default-system-prompts 1.1.4 → 1.1.5, qtap-plugin-mcp 1.1.22 → 1.1.23, qtap-plugin-openrouter 1.0.31 → 1.0.32, qtap-plugin-search-serper 1.0.7 → 1.0.8.
- **React 19 / Next 16 lint compliance — hoist function declarations (commit 1 of 5)**: The Next 16 + React 19 toolchain added strict `react-hooks/immutability` and `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect` rules that together surfaced 98 pre-existing errors. This commit knocks out the 19 `immutability` violations by moving `const fetchX = async () => {...}` declarations above the `useEffect` hooks that call them — purely mechanical, no semantic changes. 16 files touched (aurora/salon/generate-image pages plus chat/search/tools components). Net lint delta: 98 → 87 errors.
- **React 19 / Next 16 lint compliance — justified SSR exemptions for storage reads (commit 2 of 5)**: The three `set-state-in-effect` errors that were actually intentional post-hydration storage reads (localStorage for content width and quick-hide preferences, sessionStorage for auto-lock return state) now carry `// eslint-disable-next-line` directives with a clear SSR-safety justification. Lazy `useState` initializers would have caused server/client hydration mismatches because the server has no access to browser storage. (`components/providers/content-width-provider.tsx`, `components/providers/quick-hide-provider.tsx`, `app/unlock/page.tsx`) Net lint delta: 87 → 84 errors.
- **React 19 / Next 16 lint compliance — adopt SWR for fetch-on-mount (commit 3 of 5)**: Added `swr@^2.4.1` as a dependency, registered a shared `swrFetcher` (`lib/swr-fetcher.ts`) at the app root via `<SWRConfig>` in `components/providers/session-provider.tsx`, and migrated ~40 client components/hooks from `useState + useEffect + fetch(...)` patterns to `useSWR`. Mutation sites that used to call local `fetchX()` after a POST/PATCH/DELETE now call SWR's `mutate()` (with optimistic updates where appropriate, e.g. the Aurora character favorite toggle). The migration also collapses three separate `useEffect` hooks in the session provider (initial fetch, interval refetch, focus refetch) into SWR's native `refreshInterval`/`revalidateOnFocus` options where it was safe; the session provider itself keeps its bespoke 503-retry loop untouched. Two unit-test suites (`tasks-queue-card.test.tsx`, `image-gallery-deleted-handling.test.tsx`) gained `<SWRConfig value={{ provider: () => new Map() }}>` wrappers so each test gets a fresh SWR cache. Net lint delta: 84 → 69 errors (set-state-in-effect: 81 → 66). All 5213 tests green.
- **React 19 / Next 16 lint compliance — prop-mirror, modal-reset, and justified exemptions (commit 4 of 5)**: The remaining `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect` errors fell into three buckets: (a) SWR-to-local-state sync effects that couldn't be collapsed to direct derivation because the local state is also mutated by action handlers (delete/filter/toggle); (b) modal-reset useEffects where parents render modals unconditionally and rely on `isOpen` prop toggling (so conditional remounting would require broader refactors); (c) prop-mirror useEffects where downstream editable state must re-sync when upstream identity changes (e.g., `ChatRenameModal` re-syncs its `title` when `currentTitle` prop changes). Where direct derivation (`useMemo`) was feasible — `useChatControls`, `useLLMLogs`, `useStoryBackground`, `app/salon/page.tsx`, `app/aurora/page.tsx` — it was applied. Where the pattern was genuinely needed, each offending `setX(…)` call now carries an `// eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/set-state-in-effect -- <one of seven taxonomized justifications>` directly above the call (not above the `useEffect`, where the rule doesn't fire). The session provider's bespoke 503-retry loop is justified separately. Net lint delta: 69 → 3 errors; all 41 `set-state-in-effect` violations now resolved. All 5213 tests green.
- **React 19 / Next 16 lint compliance — memoization & deps fixes (commit 5 of 5)**: The final three errors and fourteen warnings. `useOutfit.ts` extracts `characterIds.length` as a stable dep in place of the non-simple `characterIds.join(',')` expression that the new `react-hooks/use-memo` rule rejects. `useNewChat.ts:232` and `useTasksQueue.ts:141` shed their outer `useCallback` wrappers entirely — React Compiler auto-memoises better than hand-written deps, and the `preserve-manual-memoization` rule was firing because the listed deps no longer matched what the compiler infers. Five `const x = data?.x ?? []` defaults (`useLLMLogs`, `AddCharacterDialog`, `outfit-selector`) are now wrapped in `useMemo` so consumer `useEffect`/`useMemo`/`useCallback` dep arrays stay stable across renders. Three missing dependencies (`isLoading`, `selectedConnectionProfileId`, `formData.provider`) were added (or justified via inline eslint-disable for intentional one-shot initialization). Two stale `eslint-disable` directives removed. The one remaining `react-hooks/incompatible-library` warning (the `useVirtualizer` call from `@tanstack/react-virtual` at `app/salon/[id]/page.tsx:470` — a library the React Compiler cannot analyze) gets its own inline eslint-disable with justification. Lint is now **completely clean** (0 errors, 0 warnings); the 98-error pile that Next 16 + React 19 surfaced in `b8f0d201` is gone. 5213 tests green.
